entries.reviewSummary: Cites the Missouri Continuing Health Improvement Act, designates MO HealthNet and the MO HealthNet division, and provides rulemaking authority.

headings.title: Short title and statutory citation
headings.reviewNote: Designates listed sections as the Missouri Continuing Health Improvement Act; source notes record sections 135.575, 192.632, and 208.975 were later repealed.

headings.title: Designation of MO HealthNet and division name
headings.reviewNote: Establishes MO HealthNet as the Title XIX medical assistance program and updates division naming conventions.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority of MO HealthNet division
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to promulgate rules and emergency rules to implement the act.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance and severability conditions
headings.reviewNote: Conditions rule validity on compliance with chapter 536 and sets nonseverability provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits unlawfully present aliens from receiving state or local public benefits with specified exceptions, requires affirmative proof or a sworn affidavit for temporary benefits, mandates federal verification, exempts IRS-registered nonprofits, and requires agency documentation assistance.

headings.title: Prohibition on public benefits for unlawful aliens
headings.reviewNote: Bars unlawfully present aliens from state or local public benefits with specified emergency care exceptions.

headings.title: Definition of public benefit and exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Defines public benefits and excludes postsecondary education, municipal permits, utility contracts, and unemployment compensation.

headings.title: Affirmative proof of citizenship or lawful presence
headings.reviewNote: Requires adult applicants to provide affirmative documentation verifying United States citizenship or lawful presence.

headings.title: Sworn affidavit for temporary public benefits
headings.reviewNote: Permits an applicant lacking required proof to sign an affidavit under oath attesting to U.S. citizenship or permanent residence with SSN and fraud-penalty explanation to receive temporary benefits or ID.

headings.title: Duration of temporary benefits and pending birth certificate
headings.reviewNote: Limits temporary benefits under a subsection 4 affidavit to ninety days (or until unlawful presence is determined) or indefinitely while a completed birth certificate application is pending.

headings.title: Federal verification of alien lawful presence
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits providing state or local public benefits to an alien until lawful presence is verified by the federal government, requiring DHS cooperation and permitting SAVE program verification.

headings.title: Exemption for IRS-registered nonprofit organizations
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not require any IRS-registered nonprofit organization to enforce it and does not prohibit such organizations from providing aid.

headings.title: Agency assistance in obtaining documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires public-benefit-administering agencies to assist applicants who sign a subsection 4 affidavit in obtaining required subsection 3 documentation.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs public assistance and MO HealthNet eligibility determinations, disqualifying resource transfers and limits, household income, burial lot and funeral trust exclusions, spousal impoverishment asset division, home disregard, Medicare Part B reimbursement, and institutionalized spouse income diversion.

headings.title: Determination of eligibility on case-by-case basis
headings.reviewNote: Requires public assistance eligibility and amount to be determined based on each individual case's facts.

headings.title: Disqualifications based on property and income limits
headings.reviewNote: Lists grounds for benefit ineligibility including excess assets, property transfers, and income.

headings.title: Consideration of household relative income and resources
headings.reviewNote: Requires considering income, resources, support, and maintenance of relatives or others living in the home to the extent allowed by federal law for federally aided programs.

headings.title: Exclusion of burial lots, prearranged funerals, and funeral trusts
headings.reviewNote: Excludes burial lots (defined), irrevocable chapter 436 prearranged funeral contracts, assigned life insurance policies, and up to $9,999 in irrevocable personal funeral trusts, requiring state reimbursement of refunds or unused funds.

headings.title: Disregard of life insurance and funeral contracts up to $1,500
headings.reviewNote: Disregards life insurance policies or prearranged funeral contracts paying $1,500 or less upon death of a claimant or living spouse (or per family member for TANF funeral contracts).

headings.title: Spousal impoverishment asset assessment and division
headings.reviewNote: Directs FSD compliance with 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5 beginning September 30, 1989, providing resource assessments, equal allocation, minimum $12,000 CPI-adjusted community spouse allowance, and post-eligibility resource protection.

headings.title: Federal asset-transfer ineligibility for institutionalized individuals
headings.reviewNote: Provides that beginning July 1, 1989, institutionalized individuals shall be ineligible for the periods and reasons specified in 42 U.S.C. Section 1396p.

headings.title: Hearings under federal spousal impoverishment law
headings.reviewNote: Requires hearings mandated by 42 U.S.C. Section 1396r-5 to be conducted pursuant to section 208.080.

headings.title: Disregard of sheltering home and regulatory definition
headings.reviewNote: Disregards an applicant's or recipient's home providing shelter to the person, spouse, or dependent child beginning October 1, 1989, and directs FSD to define by rule when a home counts as a resource.

headings.title: Reimbursement of Medicare Part B deductibles and coinsurance
headings.reviewNote: Requires Medicaid reimbursement for dual-eligible recipients to pay full Medicare Part B deductibles and coinsurance, except for hospital outpatient services or applicable Title XIX cost sharing.

headings.title: Definition of community spouse
headings.reviewNote: Defines community spouse as the noninstitutionalized spouse.

headings.title: Mandatory diversion of institutionalized spouse income
headings.reviewNote: Requires an institutionalized spouse applying for Medicaid to divert income to raise the community spouse's income to the 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5 minimum monthly needs allowance before retaining excess assets.

entries.reviewSummary: Excludes Nazi persecution restitution, seized property returns, pre-1945 insurance payments, and accrued interest from state public assistance eligibility calculations for victims and first-recipient family members, and defines Nazi persecution.

headings.title: Exclusion of Nazi restitution payments from resources
headings.reviewNote: Excludes restitution payments made to victims of Nazi persecution from eligibility resource and income calculations.

headings.title: Limitation to victims and first-recipient family members
headings.reviewNote: Restricts the exclusion to victims of Nazi persecution, actions, or policies, or their spouses or descendants who are the first recipients of the amounts, returns, or payments.

headings.title: Definition of National Socialist persecution, actions, and policies
headings.reviewNote: Defines National Socialist (Nazi) persecution, actions, and policies as those taken by Germany and other countries, or organizations, institutions, and companies therein, against Holocaust victims.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs granting general relief benefits, excludes SSI and specified categorical assistance recipients, bars unemployability based on school attendance, protects December 1973 recipients, excludes employable claimants and supported households with specified relatives, and caps monthly relief at $100.

headings.title: Granting of general relief benefits to eligible persons
headings.reviewNote: Directs the family support division to grant general relief benefits according to statutory standards.

headings.title: Ineligibility of SSI and categorical assistance recipients
headings.reviewNote: Bars general relief for persons approved for federal SSI (unless on December 1973 rolls) or receiving AFDC, aid to the blind, blind pension, or supplemental aid to the blind.

headings.title: Exclusion of school attendance from unemployability
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a person shall not be considered unemployable under this section if unemployability is due to school attendance.

headings.title: Grandfathered general relief for December 1973 SSI recipients
headings.reviewNote: Continues general relief grants for December 1973 recipients who qualify for SSI if needed to prevent reducing their December 1973 total cash income, within statutory limits.

headings.title: Ineligibility of employable claimants and specified relatives definition
headings.reviewNote: Bars general relief if the claimant is employable or if employed specified relatives (spouse, parents, siblings, children, grandparents, and their spouses) in the home have sufficient income.

headings.title: One hundred dollar monthly cap on general relief
headings.reviewNote: Caps general relief paid to an unemployable person at one hundred dollars per month.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes a farmers' market SNAP fresh food matching pilot program (up to $10/week), defines farmers' market, provides automatic vendor reimbursement, allows grants and donations, mandates rulemaking, and sets a 2027 sunset and 2028 termination.

headings.title: Establishment of farmers' market SNAP pilot program
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish a pilot program enabling SNAP participants to buy fresh food at farmers' markets.

headings.title: Definition of farmers' market
headings.reviewNote: Defines farmers' market as a multiple-stall market at a central or fixed location where farmer-producers sell agricultural products directly to the public.

headings.title: Automatic matching funds reimbursement to vendor accounts
headings.reviewNote: Provides that approved fresh food purchases by SNAP participants automatically trigger department matching funds reimbursement into central farmers' market vendor accounts.

headings.title: Appropriations, grants, gifts, and donations for funding
headings.reviewNote: Makes pilot funding subject to appropriation and permits the department to apply for grants and accept gifts, grants, and donations.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for farmers' market pilot
headings.reviewNote: Grants authority to adopt rules implementing the pilot program subject to chapter 536 requirements.

headings.title: Sunset and program termination provisions
headings.reviewNote: Sets automatic sunset six years after August 28, 2021 (August 28, 2027) and termination September 1, 2028 unless reauthorized under section 23.253.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates the treatment of proceeds from involuntary conversion of real property for public assistance eligibility.

headings.title: One-year resource exemption for involuntary conversions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that proceeds from involuntary conversion of real into personal property do not affect eligibility for one year.

headings.title: Definition of receipt of conversion proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Defines receipt as actual receipt or payment into court, except in condemnation cases where the condemning authority files an initial exception, in which case receipt means an award under final judgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits TANF and SNAP EBT transactions at restricted venues or for restricted items, imposes vendor fines, temporarily suspends benefits after 90 days of no in-state EBT use following 60-day notice, and defines EBT transaction, liquor store, and gaming exclusions.

headings.title: Prohibited establishments for electronic benefit transactions
headings.reviewNote: Bars TANF and SNAP recipients from using EBT cards in liquor stores, casinos, gaming venues, and adult clubs.

headings.title: Prohibition on vendor acceptance and graduated fines
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits store owners or proprietors from knowingly accepting EBT cards for prohibited items or at restricted venues, clarifies no general payment-source check duty for nonrestricted stores, and sets fines of up to $500, $500-$1,000, and $1,000+.

headings.title: Temporary EBT suspension after ninety days without in-state use
headings.reviewNote: Suspends EBT payments after ninety days without an in-state transaction pending residency investigation, directs case closure triggering section 208.238 if nonresident, and allows section 208.080 appeal.

headings.title: Sixty-day advance warning notice prior to suspension
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying recipients who have no in-state EBT transaction for sixty days of possible fund suspension if no in-state transaction occurs within thirty days.

headings.title: Definitions and grocery or incidental gaming exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Defines electronic benefit transfer transaction and liquor store (excluding grocery stores) and excludes grocery stores and incidental gaming establishments from casinos and gaming establishments.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Strengthening Missouri Families Act, defines TANF work activities, requires pre-eligibility work engagement, sets face-to-face sanction and cure procedures, preserves support services, disregards new-spouse income for six months, and mandates rulemaking; source note records 2015 S.B. 24 veto override.

headings.title: Citation of Strengthening Missouri Families Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 208.026, 208.040, 208.067, and 208.244 as the Strengthening Missouri Families Act.

headings.title: Work activity definitions and acceptable categories
headings.reviewNote: Defines qualifying work activities including employment, job search, vocational training, and community service.

headings.title: Work participation requirement for TANF recipients
headings.reviewNote: Requires work-eligible TANF recipients to engage in approved work activities to maintain assistance eligibility.

headings.title: Face-to-face meeting, fifty-percent sanction, cure, and closure
headings.reviewNote: Requires a face-to-face meeting and six-week cure window before a 50% benefit sanction for up to ten weeks, allowing cure via 30 hours/week work activities for one month or else case closure.

headings.title: Work activity requirement to return after sanction closure
headings.reviewNote: Requires a person sanctioned off the TANF caseload under subsection 4 to complete work activities averaging at least 30 hours/week within one month of the eligibility interview to return.

headings.title: Permitted child care and support services during sanction
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies this section does not prohibit providing child care or related support services to a financially eligible person whose cash assistance is withheld for work noncooperation.

headings.title: Six-month income and asset disregard upon marriage
headings.reviewNote: Provides a once-in-a-lifetime six-consecutive-month disregard of a new spouse's income and assets when a TANF recipient marries.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and severability provisions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes implementation rules under chapter 536 with standard nonseverability terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides for drug screening and urinalysis testing of TANF applicants and recipients based on reasonable suspicion.

headings.title: Drug screening and five-panel testing on reasonable cause
headings.reviewNote: Requires screening and five-panel urine testing of TANF applicants or recipients upon reasonable cause, imposing three-year ineligibility for positive tests or refusals unless completing approved treatment and six drug-free months.

headings.title: Administrative hearing rights for contested results
headings.reviewNote: Allows applicants or recipients testing positive or refusing tests to request an administrative hearing.

headings.title: Mandatory child abuse reporting by case workers
headings.reviewNote: Requires caseworkers to report suspected child abuse to the children's division upon positive tests or test refusals.

headings.title: Protective payee benefits for remaining household members
headings.reviewNote: Permits eligible family members to continue receiving benefits via a protective third-party payee.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking for drug screening and testing
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate screening and testing rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 compliance and nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2014.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes supplemental welfare assistance eligibility, payment calculation formulas, and residential facility payments.

headings.title: Monthly supplemental payments for December 1973 recipients
headings.reviewNote: Mandates supplemental payments to Missouri residents eligible for state assistance programs in December 1973.

headings.title: Supplemental payments for federal SSI recipients
headings.reviewNote: Calculates supplemental amounts for SSI recipients to match December 1973 income levels and protects against reduction.

headings.title: Supplemental assistance for non-SSI eligible individuals
headings.reviewNote: Provides supplemental payments for individuals meeting 1973 state criteria who do not qualify for federal SSI.

headings.title: Supplemental payments under aid to the blind standards
headings.reviewNote: Directs monthly payments to blind individuals based on 1973 statutory standards less federal SSI amounts.

headings.title: Supplemental benefits for licensed care facility residents
headings.reviewNote: Directs monthly payments for eligible non-Medicaid residents age 21+ in licensed residential care, assisted living (subject to appropriation; source note records 'appropriations' in H.B. 402), intermediate care, or skilled nursing facilities ($390 cap) plus personal needs allowance.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs development of a TANF and SNAP transitional benefits program stepping down monthly benefits from 100% to 20% between 138% and 200% FPL (capped at $5,822 monthly income), exempts transitional benefits from TANF lifetime limits, and authorizes rulemaking.

headings.title: TANF and SNAP transitional benefits program
headings.reviewNote: Directs DSS, subject to appropriations and waivers, to implement a TANF and SNAP transitional benefits program preventing abrupt benefit loss when income exceeds program maximums.

headings.title: Step-down benefit schedule and monthly income cap
headings.reviewNote: Sets gradual benefit reductions from 100% (<=138% FPL; source note records 'thirty-eighty' in S.B. 106) down to 20% (190%-200% FPL) and disqualifies households exceeding $5,822 monthly income adjusted for inflation.

headings.title: Program compliance and exclusion from TANF lifetime limit
headings.reviewNote: Requires transitional benefit recipients to meet program work and other requirements while excluding transitional benefits from the section 208.040 TANF lifetime limit.

headings.title: Permissive rulemaking authority and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Permits DSS to promulgate implementation rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 compliance and nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2023.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs Temporary Assistance (TANF) eligibility, SSN, support assignment, and cooperation conditions, minor parent living requirements, welfare-to-work policies including the 45-month lifetime limit, cash diversion, and personal responsibility plans, uniform standards, and 1996 eligibility floors; source note records 2015 S.B. 24 veto override.

headings.title: Eligibility criteria for dependent children and caregivers
headings.reviewNote: Specifies age, residence, deprivation of parental support, and living arrangements required for TANF eligibility.

headings.title: SSN, support assignment, paternity, third-party, and program cooperation
headings.reviewNote: Requires TANF applicants and recipients to furnish SSNs, assign support rights by operation of law, cooperate in establishing paternity and identifying liable medical third parties, and participate in welfare-reduction programs.

headings.title: Adult-supervised living requirement for unmarried minor parents
headings.reviewNote: Requires unmarried pregnant or parenting minors under 18 to live with a parent, guardian, adult relative, or supervised living arrangement with four federal exceptions and earned income disregard up to 100% FPL.

headings.title: Protective payments for children when relative refuses cooperation
headings.reviewNote: Directs paying eligible child benefits under section 208.180(2) when a caretaker relative is ineligible for refusing support or paternity cooperation under subsection 2(3).

headings.title: Welfare-reduction policies, 45-month limit, cash diversion, and orientation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rules for two-thirds earned income disregards, postsecondary education as work activity, biennial legislative reports, wage supplementation, the 45-month TANF lifetime limit (from Jan 1, 2016), lump-sum cash diversion, and orientation with personal responsibility plans.

headings.title: Exemption from unemployed parent work history rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that work history requirements and the definition of unemployed shall not apply to parents for eligibility under section 208.041.

headings.title: Uniform statewide eligibility and benefit standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to continue applying uniform eligibility and benefit standards across all political subdivisions, except pilot projects.

headings.title: July 16, 1996 income and resource eligibility floor
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, consistent with federal law, to maintain income and resource eligibility requirements no more restrictive than those of July 16, 1996.

entries.reviewSummary: Extends dependent children benefits to children of unemployed parents, sets unemployment and work-quarter eligibility conditions, mandates interagency education and employment security agreements, prorates payments within appropriations, and sets a June 16, 1983 effective date.

headings.title: Assistance to children of unemployed parents
headings.reviewNote: Extends dependent children benefits to families where a parent is unemployed and meets federal work history criteria.

headings.title: Cooperative agreements for vocational rehabilitation and education
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to enter cooperative agreements with DESE and the Coordinating Board for Higher Education for public vocational rehabilitation and education training of unemployed parents.

headings.title: Employment security registration and Secretary of Labor referral
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to contract with the division of employment security for registration and refer unemployed parents to the U.S. Secretary of Labor within thirty days for section 208.042 work programs.

headings.title: Proration of payments within appropriation limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires payments to be prorated within appropriation limits and prohibits exceeding appropriated amounts.

headings.title: Delayed effective date of June 16, 1983
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section shall not become effective until June 16, 1983.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires referral of eligible AFDC household members age 16+ to federal work incentive and training programs, sets referral standards and four exemptions, governs state cost shares and expense allowances, limits payments upon refusal, and authorizes child day care funding.

headings.title: Referral of AFDC household members to federal work programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to refer appropriate AFDC children, relatives, or eligible individuals age 16+ to the U.S. Secretary of Labor for employment, training, work incentive, or special work projects.

headings.title: Referral standards and exemptions from work participation
headings.reviewNote: Directs FSD to set referral standards prohibiting refusal without good cause while exempting ill, incapacitated, or aged persons, remote residents, full-time school children, and essential household caregivers.

headings.title: State cost-sharing payments and participant expense allowances
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to pay up to 20% of work incentive program costs and special work project amounts within maximums, and permits additional allowances for reasonable participant work training expenses.

headings.title: Payment restrictions upon refusal without good cause
headings.reviewNote: Limits continued payments to 60 days via section 208.180(2) when a child or relative refuses work participation without good cause, and directs protective payments for children cared for by a refusing relative.

headings.title: Authorization for child day care expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes FSD to expend funds to provide appropriate child day care required by adult absence due to work or training participation.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants aid to dependent children living with a legal guardian who is not an eligible relative under section 208.040 and sets monthly benefits by section 208.150 standards.

headings.title: Eligibility of dependent children living with legal guardians
headings.reviewNote: Grants AFDC benefits on behalf of a needy child under 18 deprived of parental support and living with a legal guardian who is ineligible under section 208.040 because the guardian is not a specified relative.

headings.title: Determination of monthly benefit amount under section 208.150
headings.reviewNote: Requires monthly public assistance benefits under this section to be determined by the standards set forth in section 208.150.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires DESE to provide child day care services to persons qualifying under the federal Family Support Act of 1988 via direct payments to licensed or license-exempt providers and permits continued eligibility after twelve-month transitional day care ends.

headings.title: Child day care services under federal Family Support Act
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE to provide child day care services to any person meeting qualifications under sections 301 and 302 of the Family Support Act of 1988 (P.L. 100-485).

headings.title: Direct payments to licensed and small license-exempt providers
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE to purchase child day care by direct payments to chapter 210 licensed providers or providers exempt from licensing under section 210.211 caring for no more than six children.

headings.title: Continued day care eligibility after twelve-month transitional period
headings.reviewNote: Permits a person whose twelve-month transitional day care under section 208.400 ends to receive day care services from DESE if otherwise eligible.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes sliding fee scale child care subsidies, copayment waivers for special needs, and definitions.

headings.title: Sliding fee scale rules and special needs fee waiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE to promulgate rules modifying child care income eligibility with an appropriation-subject sliding fee scale, reduced transitional subsidies, special needs fee waivers, and maximum payment formulas.

headings.title: Definition of annual appropriation level
headings.reviewNote: Defines annual appropriation level as the maximum income threshold for full child care benefit eligibility.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and severability conditions
headings.reviewNote: Delegates rulemaking authority under chapter 536 subject to nonseverability provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes aid to dependent children in foster family homes or private child care institutions.

headings.title: Eligibility for children in foster care placement
headings.reviewNote: Extends aid to dependent children placed in foster homes or private institutions following judicial removal.

headings.title: Maximum monthly benefit limit and federal funding condition
headings.reviewNote: Caps monthly foster care benefits at one hundred dollars and conditions payments on federal funding availability.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires secondary school attendance for eighteen-year-old dependent children to retain assistance eligibility.

headings.title: School attendance requirement for eighteen-year-old dependents
headings.reviewNote: Requires eighteen-year-old dependent children to be full-time secondary or vocational students to retain aid.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority for school attendance
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of social services to promulgate rules implementing school attendance requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes transitional child care subsidy benefits program, reporting obligations, and waiver requirements.

headings.title: Establishment of transitional child care subsidy program
headings.reviewNote: Creates a tiered sliding-scale child care subsidy program for households exceeding full benefit income thresholds.

headings.title: Annual reporting to the general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual legislative report on program participant counts, employment effectiveness, and administrative costs.

headings.title: Pursuit of federal waivers for program execution
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to apply for federal waivers needed to implement transitional child care subsidies.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and severability provisions
headings.reviewNote: Delegates rulemaking authority under chapter 536 and includes nonseverability terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires Title IV-A and Title XIX public assistance applicants and recipients to cooperate in establishing paternity and support, assigns Title IV-A support rights to the state by operation of law, and defines public assistance.

headings.title: Paternity cooperation and assignment of child support rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires Title IV-A and Title XIX applicants and recipients to cooperate in good faith in paternity and support enforcement (subject to good cause exceptions) and assigns Title IV-A support rights to the state by operation of law.

headings.title: Definition of public assistance and exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Defines public assistance as income support benefits including money, institutional care, or shelter (except temporary shelter) and Title IV-A programs, excluding noncash and short-term benefits.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires a competitively bid contract for initial and ongoing SNAP, TANF, child care, and MO HealthNet eligibility data matching, quarterly asset reviews and monthly status checks, DSS final determinations within twenty business days, and an annual joint legislative report.

headings.title: Competitively bid contract for eligibility data matching
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS by January 1, 2017 to contract for initial and ongoing data matching of SNAP, TANF, child care, and MO HealthNet applicants and recipients against public records and other data sources.

headings.title: Quarterly asset reviews and monthly status identification
headings.reviewNote: Requires the contractor to evaluate income, resources, and assets at least quarterly and monthly identify participants who died, moved out of state, or were incarcerated over ninety days.

headings.title: Notification, long-term care exception, and twenty-day determination
headings.reviewNote: Requires contractor verification notices (excluding compliant long-term care and HCBS recipients), mandates DSS eligibility determinations within twenty business days while retaining final authority, and requires contractor recordkeeping.

headings.title: Annual joint report to governor and legislative leaders
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS and the contractor within thirty days after each calendar year to file a joint report detailing ineligibility determinations and stated reasons.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires one-page initial application and periodic eligibility review forms for SNAP, TANF, child care, and MO HealthNet, permits attaching review forms to Missouri income tax returns, mandates DOR sharing with DSS, and authorizes DOR rulemaking.

headings.title: One-page initial public assistance application form
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS, upon federal approval, to limit initial SNAP, TANF, child care, and MO HealthNet applications to an accessible one-page website form; source note records 'Unites' in S.B. 106 (2023).

headings.title: One-page periodic review form and tax return attachment
headings.reviewNote: Permits program participants to attach periodic eligibility review forms to their Missouri individual income tax returns and requires DSS to limit such forms to one page on DSS and DOR websites.

headings.title: Department of Revenue sharing of eligibility forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Department of Revenue, notwithstanding section 32.057, to share any eligibility form submitted under this section with DSS.

headings.title: Department of Revenue rulemaking authority and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Permits DOR to promulgate administration rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 compliance and nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2023.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires setting aside at least two percent of federal TANF Block Grant funds for alternatives to abortion programs and two percent for healthy marriage and responsible fatherhood activities to supplement, not supplant, other revenues; source note records 2015 S.B. 24 veto override.

headings.title: Minimum two-percent TANF set-asides for designated programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS, subject to appropriation and federal law, to set aside at least 2% of TANF block grant funds for alternatives to abortion programs and 2% for healthy marriage and responsible fatherhood activities, preferring qualifying nonprofits.

headings.title: Intent to supplement rather than supplant existing revenue
headings.reviewNote: Declares legislative intent that funding authorized under this section supplement, not supplant, other revenue sources used for these purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Guarantees the right to apply for public assistance with reasonable promptness, allows in-person, phone, or mail applications, requires prompt investigation and notice, sets verification duties and a 45-day default timeline, and requires explaining all available assistance categories.

headings.title: Right to apply and prompt furnishing of assistance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to permit any individual to apply for temporary or other department-administered public assistance and to furnish assistance with reasonable promptness.

headings.title: Methods for requesting assistance at county office
headings.reviewNote: Permits requests for assistance to be made at a county FSD office in person, by telephone, or by mail.

headings.title: Prompt investigation, eligibility decision, and applicant notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD upon receiving a request to promptly investigate circumstances, decide eligibility, benefit amount, and start date, and notify the applicant.

headings.title: Division verification duties and applicant protections
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD during application or recertification to provide clear written cooperation instructions, assist in verification, avoid duplicate proof requests, and not deny solely due to third-party noncooperation.

headings.title: Investigation completion timelines and forty-five-day default
headings.reviewNote: Requires completing investigations within federal or state statutory limits, or providing benefits within forty-five days of application if no time limit is specified.

headings.title: Explanation of benefit categories and alternative eligibility evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Requires explaining all available assistance categories and TANF consequences (lifetime limits, work rules), and evaluating medical, food stamp, and other eligibility if the applicant declines TANF.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires individualized employability assessments for qualifying recipients before assignment to welfare-to-work components consistent with section 208.325, and authorizes chapter 536 rulemaking.

headings.title: Individualized skills and employability assessment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to make an individualized assessment of skills, prior work experience, and employability for each recipient who is age 18+ or has not completed high school or equivalency and is not attending secondary school.

headings.title: Assessment prerequisite before welfare-to-work assignment
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits assigning any participant to education, training, or employment welfare-to-work components prior to an individualized assessment consistent with section 208.325.

headings.title: Permissive rulemaking authority under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Permits the division to promulgate reasonable and necessary rules for this section, effective only when promulgated under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires approving or denying completed medical assistance applications within thirty days, remitting nursing home Medicaid payments within forty-five days of admission, and accepting applications from responsible persons for minors or incapacitated applicants.

headings.title: Thirty-day deadline for medical assistance applications
headings.reviewNote: Requires approving or denying a completed application for section 208.152 medical assistance within thirty days of submission to FSD or its successor.

headings.title: Forty-five-day Medicaid payment for newly admitted nursing residents
headings.reviewNote: Requires the MO HealthNet division to remit Medicaid payment to a licensed nursing home operator for a newly admitted Medicaid resident within forty-five days of admission.

headings.title: Applications on behalf of minors or incapacitated persons
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD or its successor, under 42 CFR 435.907(a), to accept an application from someone acting responsibly for a minor or incapacitated applicant.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires medical examinations and permits reexaminations for physical or mental incapacity benefit claims, and makes written medical reports competent, admissible prima facie evidence in section 208.080 appeal hearings.

headings.title: Required initial medical examinations and discretionary reexaminations
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD-designated medical examination for AFDC or PTD physical/mental condition applications, permits reexaminations as needed, and requires evaluating written reports.

headings.title: Admissibility and prima facie execution of medical reports on appeal
headings.reviewNote: Makes FSD-designated examination reports and claimant-submitted physician or clinic reports competent, admissible evidence at section 208.080 hearings and prima facie properly executed without further identification.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes administrative appeal rights to FSD, CD, or MO HealthNet division directors, ten-day pre-action appeals with continuing benefits, ninety-day post-closure and rejection appeals, county-of-residence fair hearings, and written findings and conclusions.

headings.title: Right to appeal division benefit or service decisions
headings.reviewNote: Permits applicants or recipients to appeal to the FSD, CD, or MO HealthNet director for denied application rights, disallowed or delayed applications, proposed cancellations/modifications, adverse determinations, or protective payee decisions.

headings.title: Evidentiary scope for termination or modification appeals
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director's decision on a termination or modification appeal to be based on facts shown at the hearing to have existed when the action was proposed or taken.

headings.title: Ten-day appeal of proposed action and continuing benefits
headings.reviewNote: Grants ten days from mailing of notice to appeal proposed reductions, modifications, or discontinuances with benefits continuing undiminished (unless an AFDC recipient opts out); source note records 'the the' in original rolls.

headings.title: Ninety-day post-closure appeal without continuing benefits
headings.reviewNote: Grants ninety days from case closing or modification to appeal when no prior appeal was requested, requiring notice and forms without continuing prior benefit levels during the appeal.

headings.title: Ninety-day appeal of application rejection
headings.reviewNote: Grants aggrieved applicants ninety days from notice of application rejection to appeal, requiring appeal-rights notice, blank forms, and immediate transmission.

headings.title: Evidentiary scope for application rejection appeals
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director's decision on a rejection appeal to be based on facts shown at the hearing to have existed at the time of rejection.

headings.title: County fair hearing, evidence record, and written decision
headings.reviewNote: Requires reasonable notice and a fair hearing in the claimant's county of residence with counsel, witnesses, preserved record, and a decision stating findings of fact and conclusions of law.

headings.title: Transcription and signing of oral or written appeal requests
headings.reviewNote: Permits initial appeal requests orally or in writing, requiring transcription onto division forms signed by the aggrieved person or representative before the hearing begins.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs circuit court appeals of section 208.080 director decisions within ninety days in the claimant's county of residence, affidavit forms, fee-free docketing and record certification, record-based trial, and section 536.140 review.

headings.title: Ninety-day appeal to claimant's county circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Permits any claimant aggrieved by a section 208.080 director decision to appeal to the circuit court of the claimant's county of residence within ninety days.

headings.title: Division furnishing of appeal affidavit form
headings.reviewNote: Requires the appropriate division, upon request, to furnish the claimant with the proper affidavit form for appealing to circuit court.

headings.title: Filing of affidavit, record certification, and fee-free docketing
headings.reviewNote: Requires certifying the preserved record, decision, and executed affidavit to circuit court upon filing within ninety days and docketing as a civil case without bond or docket fee.

headings.title: Trial on certified administrative record
headings.reviewNote: Requires trying the appeal in circuit court upon the record of proceedings had before and certified by the division director.

headings.title: Section 536.140 review and authorized circuit court judgments
headings.reviewNote: Requires reviewing the director's decision under section 536.140 and entering judgment affirming, reversing, or modifying it, with authority to order reconsideration or further proper action.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes supplemental reimbursement for ground emergency medical transportation service providers under MO HealthNet.

headings.title: Supplemental payments for ground emergency medical transport
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes supplemental MO HealthNet payments to eligible government-owned ground emergency medical providers.

headings.title: Eligibility criteria for emergency transport providers
headings.reviewNote: Defines qualifying providers as government entities providing emergency medical ground transport to MO HealthNet patients.

headings.title: Calculation of allowable supplemental reimbursement amount
headings.reviewNote: Calculates supplemental payments up to actual certified costs of providing emergency medical transportation.

headings.title: Administrative cost reimbursement agreement and governmental share
headings.reviewNote: Requires eligible providers to maintain an agreement reimbursing DSS administrative costs and requires governmental entities to fund and certify the nonfederal share.

headings.title: Voluntary participation and federal expenditure certification duties
headings.reviewNote: Makes participation voluntary and requires electing governmental entities to certify expenditures under 42 CFR 433.51, provide supporting evidence and data, and maintain retrievable CMS records.

headings.title: Federal approvals, FFP claim submission, and annual assurances
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DSS to seek federal approvals and limit costs to Title XIX allowable expenditures, requires submitting FFP claims, and requires annual federal allowability assurances.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes a voluntary intergovernmental transfer program for government-affiliated ground emergency medical transport providers to increase MO HealthNet managed care capitation payments, requiring 100% MCO pass-through, administrative fee reimbursement, data compliance, and federal approvals.

headings.title: Intergovernmental transfer program for managed care capitation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DSS to design and implement an IGT program with eligible providers covering ground emergency medical transport and prestabilization to increase capitation payments.

headings.title: Eligibility requirements for managed care transport providers
headings.reviewNote: Specifies criteria for participating government-affiliated emergency ground transportation providers.

headings.title: Increased capitation payments and full managed care pass-through
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to make increased capitation payments (actuarially equivalent to fee-for-service up to commercial rates) funded by voluntary IGTs, with managed care plans paying 100% of increased amounts to eligible providers.

headings.title: Implementation upon federal approval and retroactive payments
headings.reviewNote: Directs implementation on the date federal approval is obtained to the extent IGTs are provided, and requires retroactive implementation as permitted by federal law.

headings.title: Voluntary participation by transferring entities
headings.reviewNote: Declares participation in intergovernmental transfers under this section voluntary on the part of transferring entities for all applicable federal laws.

headings.title: Reimbursement of state department administrative expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating providers to reimburse state administrative costs with an administrative fee up to twenty percent.

headings.title: Provider data sharing and federal documentation compliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires managed care plans and providers to supply documentation necessary to secure federal reimbursement.

headings.title: Federal financial participation contingency
headings.reviewNote: Conditions implementation strictly on the continued availability of federal financial participation.

headings.title: Director discretion regarding noncompliant payments
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director discretion to return transfers or adjust payments to maintain compliance with federal law.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Missouri Senior Services Protection Fund, providing dedicated funding for low-income seniors and disabled persons.

headings.title: Creation of Missouri Senior Services Protection Fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri Senior Services Protection Fund as a dedicated state treasury fund that does not revert.

headings.title: Transfer of state funds and dedicated service allocations
headings.reviewNote: Directs transfer of fifty-five million one hundred thousand dollars dedicated to low-income senior and disability services.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates the transfer of prescribed long-acting reversible contraceptives between MO HealthNet participants.

headings.title: Definition of long-acting reversible contraceptive
headings.reviewNote: Defines long-acting reversible contraceptives to include intrauterine devices and hormonal birth control implants.

headings.title: Conditions for transferring unused contraceptives between participants
headings.reviewNote: Sets medical safety, packaging, and provider possession rules for transferring unused contraceptives to another participant.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs the confidentiality and disclosure of public assistance records and establishes criminal penalties for misuse.

headings.title: Confidentiality and restricted disclosure of applicant records
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits disclosure of public assistance records except for official administrative or judicial proceedings.

headings.title: Monthly county welfare inspection reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires monthly county office reports of recipient names and amounts for public inspection.

headings.title: Prohibition against commercial or political use of lists
headings.reviewNote: Makes commercial or political use of public assistance recipient lists a misdemeanor offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides MO HealthNet hospital reimbursement for medically necessary donor human breast milk for infants.

headings.title: Mandatory reimbursement criteria for donor human breast milk
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to reimburse hospitals for physician-ordered, medically necessary donor human breast milk from qualifying banks for critically ill NICU infants under three months with parental informed consent.

headings.title: Web-based prior authorization requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires prior authorization through an electronic web-based system based on national medical guidelines.

headings.title: Promulgation of rules and nonseverability conditions
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate implementation rules subject to chapter 536 nonseverability terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Imposes an eight-dollar MO HealthNet co-payment for nonemergency emergency department services without reducing provider reimbursement, defines emergency medical condition, mandates rulemaking, and directs CMS state plan amendments and waivers; source note records 2016 S.B. 608 veto override.

headings.title: Eight-dollar co-payment for nonemergency emergency department visits
headings.reviewNote: Requires an $8 co-payment beginning October 1, 2016 for nonemergency hospital emergency department visits with prior notice, clarifying participant nonpayment shall not reduce provider reimbursement.

headings.title: Prudent layperson definition of emergency medical condition
headings.reviewNote: Defines emergency medical condition using a prudent layperson standard for acute symptoms risking serious jeopardy to health or unborn child, serious impairment of bodily functions, or serious organ dysfunction.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate implementation rules (including physician documentation and parental informed consent text in source) subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2016.

headings.title: Submission of federal state plan amendments and waivers
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to submit necessary state plan amendments and waivers to CMS to implement this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Makes enrolled MO HealthNet doulas eligible to enroll with fee-for-service and managed care payers and requires fee-for-service schedule reimbursement.

headings.title: Doula eligibility to enroll with fee-for-service and managed care payers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that once enrolled as a MO HealthNet provider, a doula is eligible to enroll with MO HealthNet-affiliated fee-for-service and managed care payers.

headings.title: Fee-for-service schedule reimbursement for doula services
headings.reviewNote: Requires doula services to be reimbursed on a fee-for-service schedule.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires the family support division to determine whether Medicaid applicants or recipients qualify for Missouri Veterans Commission medical services, encourage VA utilization without requiring exhaustion, and consult with the commission on eligibility determination methods.

headings.title: Veterans medical services eligibility determination and non-exhaustion
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD under section 208.215 to determine Medicaid applicants' and recipients' eligibility for Missouri Veterans Commission medical services and encourage VA use without requiring VA benefit exhaustion.

headings.title: Consultation with Missouri Veterans Commission on eligibility methods
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to consult with the Missouri Veterans Commission regarding a method for determining VA medical benefit eligibility.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Ticket to Work Health Assurance Program for employed disabled individuals, defining earned income tax documentation, asset and income disregards, tiered premiums, change reporting, employer-sponsored insurance coordination, annual legislative reporting, and CMS state plan amendments.

headings.title: Establishment of Ticket to Work Health Assurance Program
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Ticket to Work medical assistance program for employed disabled individuals.

headings.title: Documentation of Medicare and Social Security tax withholding
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to document Medicare and Social Security tax withholding (or proof of payment for self-employed persons) for income to qualify as earned income.

headings.title: Income limits and allowable resource exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Sets net income limits and exempts retirement accounts, medical savings, and earned income.

headings.title: Sliding scale monthly premium requirements
headings.reviewNote: Establishes sliding fee premium payments based on gross earned and unearned income.

headings.title: Ten-day reporting of income or household changes and premium adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Requires recipients to report income or household size changes within ten days, applying premium increases on the next post-due-process invoice and decreases on the first of the next month.

headings.title: Employer-sponsored health insurance participation and secondary coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires participation in cost-effective employer-sponsored insurance with DSS paying employee premiums and cost sharing, limiting program coverage to secondary personal care assistance and nonemergency medical transportation.

headings.title: Annual legislative report on enrollment and outreach
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to submit an annual report to the general assembly identifying participant counts and outreach and education efforts.

headings.title: Submission of CMS state plan amendments and waivers
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to submit necessary state plan amendments and waivers to CMS to implement this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires annual FSD income and eligibility verification reviews for medical assistance recipients, permits satisfaction via periodic food stamp redetermination, sets ten-day response and appeal notice timelines, and lists acceptable income documentation.

headings.title: Annual income and eligibility verification review
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to conduct an annual income and eligibility verification review of each medical assistance recipient within twelve months of the last determination.

headings.title: Satisfaction via periodic food stamp redetermination
headings.reviewNote: Permits satisfying the annual eligibility review requirement through completion of a periodic food stamp redetermination for the household.

headings.title: Annual reverification letter, ten-day deadline, and appeal notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to send an annual reverification letter requiring response and documentation within ten days, followed by a ten-day appeal-or-closure notice upon nonresponse.

headings.title: Required income verification documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires recipients to provide income verification documentation, which may include wage stubs, W-2 forms, employer statements, employment security wage matches, and bank statements.

entries.reviewSummary: Permits fee-for-service MO HealthNet providers to charge graduated missed appointment fees ($0/$5/$10/$20 over three years) with inclement weather waivers, preserves MCO adherence incentives, bars MO HealthNet billing, and directs CMS approvals; source note records 2016 S.B. 608 veto override.

headings.title: Graduated missed appointment fees and inclement weather waiver
headings.reviewNote: Permits fee-for-service MO HealthNet providers to require payment of graduated fees ($0 first, up to $5 second, $10 third, $20 fourth+ in three years) for missed or <24-hour-canceled appointments before rescheduling, waiving fees for inclement weather.

headings.title: Preservation of managed care appointment adherence incentives
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies this section does not limit MO HealthNet managed care organizations from developing and implementing appointment adherence incentive programs.

headings.title: Prohibition on charging or reimbursing missed appointment fees
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits health care providers from charging missed appointment fees to MO HealthNet and prohibits participant reimbursement by MO HealthNet.

headings.title: Submission of CMS state plan amendments and waivers
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to submit necessary state plan amendments and waivers to CMS to implement this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines clinical pathology services, recognizes the professional component by hospital-based pathologists as distinct MO HealthNet physician services reimbursed at least 30% of the Independent Lab technical schedule, directs payment to physicians or assignees, and mandates CMS filings and chapter 536 rules.

headings.title: Definitions for clinical pathology services reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Defines clinical pathology services, hospital-based pathologist, MO HealthNet, and professional component of clinical pathology services.

headings.title: Recognition as distinct physician services
headings.reviewNote: Requires MO HealthNet to recognize the professional component of clinical pathology services provided by a hospital-based pathologist as distinct physician services.

headings.title: Mandatory MO HealthNet reimbursement of professional component
headings.reviewNote: Requires MO HealthNet to reimburse the professional component of clinical pathology services provided to MO HealthNet participants.

headings.title: Minimum thirty-percent technical fee schedule reimbursement rate
headings.reviewNote: Sets reimbursement for the professional component at no less than thirty percent of the approved MO HealthNet Independent Lab - Technical Component fee schedule.

headings.title: Direct payment to physician or assigned entity
headings.reviewNote: Requires payment to be made directly to the licensed physician providing the services or the entity assigned the right to receive payment.

headings.title: State plan amendment submission and federal approval efforts
headings.reviewNote: Requires timely submission of any needed state plan amendment and reasonable efforts to obtain federal approval while preserving DSS's obligation to implement reimbursement to the fullest lawful extent.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate administration rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2026.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines twenty-eight categories of persons eligible for MO HealthNet benefits, mandates chapter 536 rulemaking, provides transitional medical assistance and three-month retroactive coverage, limits federal waivers, conditions subdivisions 1(1)-(22) on annual appropriations, and protects military families' developmental disability eligibility.

headings.title: Eligible categories of persons for medical assistance
headings.reviewNote: Lists statutory categories of eligible persons including low-income families, elderly, blind, and disabled.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires rules implementing this section to be promulgated under chapter 536 and section 536.028 and declares nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2002.

headings.title: Transitional MO HealthNet coverage after employment earnings
headings.reviewNote: Provides transitional MO HealthNet coverage (four months pre-1990; six months plus an additional six fee-free months after April 1, 1990) for families losing cash assistance due to employment income or hours.

headings.title: Three-month retroactive medical assistance eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Makes MO HealthNet benefits available for unpaid medical expenses furnished in or after the third month before application if the individual would have been eligible when care was furnished.

headings.title: Limits on Section 1115 and additional federal waivers
headings.reviewNote: Permits DSS to seek Section 1115 or other waivers up to $1 million in added state costs unless appropriated or directed by statute, protects RHC/FQHC services unless oversight-approved, and subjects waivers to legislative disapproval.

headings.title: Annual appropriation contingency for specified eligibility groups
headings.reviewNote: Conditions eligibility under subdivisions (1) to (22) of subsection 1 on annual appropriations, excluding mandatory federal coverage groups under 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(10)(A)(i).

headings.title: Military service members' developmental disability eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Temporarily suspends and immediately restores MO HealthNet developmental disability eligibility for resident military families stationed out of state, and grants temporary eligibility to nonresident military families stationed in Missouri.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerates MO HealthNet covered services and additional benefits for children, pregnant women, and blind persons, governs co-payments, medication sampling, OB/pediatric and FQHC rates, WIC referrals, LTC rates, sheltered workshop disregards, MMAC audit change notices, CPT behavioral codes, and gender-transition payment bars.

headings.title: Covered MO HealthNet medical services and payment rules
headings.reviewNote: Lists twenty-six covered service categories and payment rules including inpatient/outpatient hospital, nursing homes, physicians (excluding abortion facilities), chiropractic, drugs, EPSDT, personal care, mental health, hospice, DME, dental, optometry, blood clotting, and hearing instruments.

headings.title: Additional benefits for children, pregnant women, and blind persons
headings.reviewNote: Provides additional MO HealthNet payments for eligible children, pregnant women, and blind persons covering dental, podiatry, optometry, prosthetics/eyeglasses/dentures/wheelchairs, hospice, and comprehensive day rehabilitation.

headings.title: Participant cost sharing, co-payments, and provider rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits MO HealthNet participant co-payments (exempting children, pregnant women, blind persons, and specified services), bars refusing service for inability to pay, and governs bad-debt policies pending CMS approval.

headings.title: Collection of medication samples for program integrity
headings.reviewNote: Grants the MO HealthNet division the right to collect medication samples from participants to maintain program integrity.

headings.title: Timely and sufficient obstetrical and pediatric reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Requires obstetrical and pediatric reimbursement to be timely and sufficient to ensure general-population access under 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(30)(A).

headings.title: Reimbursement for federally funded health centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires reimbursement for federally funded health center services beginning July 1, 1990 in accordance with P.L. 101-239 Sections 6402(c) and 6404.

headings.title: Notification and referral to WIC food programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS beginning July 1, 1990 to notify and refer MO HealthNet-eligible children under five and pregnant, breastfeeding, or postpartum women to DHSS WIC programs.

headings.title: Long-term care provider cost reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Requires reimbursing long-term care providers for costs in accordance with 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(13)(A) and federal regulations.

headings.title: Long-term care rate cap upon arm's-length ownership change
headings.reviewNote: Caps reimbursement rate increases for previously certified long-term care facilities after a total arm's-length ownership change at limits under 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(13)(C).

headings.title: Enrollment of residential care and assisted living personal care providers
headings.reviewNote: Permits the MO HealthNet division to enroll qualified chapter 198 residential care and assisted living facilities as MO HealthNet personal care providers.

headings.title: Disregard of sheltered workshop extended employment income
headings.reviewNote: Excludes income earned by individuals eligible for certified chapter 178 sheltered workshop extended employment from eligibility determinations under this section.

headings.title: Five-day MMAC advance notice of audit interpretation changes
headings.reviewNote: Requires MMAC to give five business days' written or email notice before changing reimbursement audit interpretations, waiving recoupment liability if notice is not given.

headings.title: Preservation of chapter 536 rulemaking requirement
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section abrogates or limits the department's statutory requirement to promulgate rules under chapter 536.

headings.title: Reimbursement for CPT behavioral and psychophysiological codes
headings.reviewNote: Requires reimbursing providers (including psychologists), subject to appropriations beginning July 1, 2016, for behavioral, social, and psychophysiological services for physical health using CPT codes 96150-96154.

headings.title: Prohibition on payments for gender transition procedures
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits payments under this section for gender transition surgeries, cross-sex hormones, or puberty-blocking drugs as defined in section 191.1720 for gender transition.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs MO HealthNet payment rules and third-party resource exhaustion, covers Medicare Part A and B cost sharing for QMBs, QDWIs, and SLMBs, requires cost-effective group health plan enrollment, disregards Social Security COLAs until FPL updates, and credits post-spenddown medical expenses.

headings.title: Benefit rules, third-party exhaustion, and Medicare buy-in
headings.reviewNote: Requires MO HealthNet division rules defining benefit costs and fees, mandates exhausting other entitlements and causes of action, protects choice of qualified providers, and permits paying Title XVIII B/XIX Medicare cost sharing.

headings.title: Benefit payments for qualified Medicare beneficiaries
headings.reviewNote: Includes MO HealthNet benefit payments for premiums, deductibles, and coinsurance on behalf of qualified Medicare beneficiaries under 42 U.S.C. 1396d(p).

headings.title: Medicare Part A cost sharing for qualified disabled working individuals
headings.reviewNote: Includes Medicare Part A cost-sharing payments for qualified disabled and working individuals under 42 U.S.C. 1396d(s) and permits imposing federally authorized premiums.

headings.title: Medicare Part B cost sharing for specified low-income beneficiaries
headings.reviewNote: Includes Medicare Part B cost-sharing payments for QMB-like individuals with incomes below 110% FPL (1993) and 120% FPL (1995).

headings.title: Cost-effective group health plan premium and cost-sharing payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires MO HealthNet payment of premiums and cost sharing for cost-effective group health plans under Social Security Act Section 1906, including noneligible family premiums when required and cost effective.

headings.title: Temporary disregard of Social Security cost-of-living increases
headings.reviewNote: Disregards annual Social Security cost-of-living increases until that year's federal poverty level is implemented.

headings.title: Three-month future spenddown deduction for out-of-pocket expenses
headings.reviewNote: Allows a MO HealthNet participant who paid cash spenddown to deduct subsequent out-of-pocket valid medical expenses for that month against future required spenddown for up to three months.

entries.reviewSummary: Guarantees section 208.080 fair hearings for medical assistance applicants and recipients and Administrative Hearing Commission review for MO HealthNet providers, sets a $500 claim threshold, class actions, 30- and 90-day filing deadlines, stay order conditions, and circuit court appeals.

headings.title: Applicant and recipient fair hearings under section 208.080
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD or MO HealthNet division to grant section 208.080 fair hearings to applicants or recipients whose medical assistance claims are denied or not acted upon with reasonable promptness.

headings.title: AHC hearing for denied or delayed provider reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Entitles authorized providers whose reimbursement claims are denied or not acted upon with reasonable promptness to a chapter 621 AHC hearing.

headings.title: AHC hearing for denied provider program participation
headings.reviewNote: Entitles authorized providers denied participation in any chapter 208 program to a chapter 621 AHC hearing.

headings.title: AHC hearing for providers aggrieved by department rules
headings.reviewNote: Entitles authorized providers aggrieved by any DSS or division rule or regulation to a chapter 621 AHC hearing.

headings.title: AHC hearing for providers aggrieved under section 208.166
headings.reviewNote: Entitles authorized providers aggrieved by any DSS or division rule, contractual agreement, or decision under section 208.166 to a chapter 621 AHC hearing.

headings.title: Five-hundred-dollar minimum reimbursement threshold
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a provider from filing an AHC hearing petition unless the reimbursement amount sought exceeds five hundred dollars.

headings.title: Class action hearings for similarly situated providers
headings.reviewNote: Permits one or more adequately representative providers to institute an AHC hearing on behalf of a class sharing common questions of law or fact and seeking common relief.

headings.title: Thirty-day filing deadline and accumulation of smaller claims
headings.reviewNote: Sets a thirty-day filing deadline from mailing or delivery of a decision, allowing claims under $500 to be accumulated until reaching $500 with ninety days to file.

headings.title: Full-hearing, bond, and federal funding prerequisites for stay orders
headings.reviewNote: Bars AHC stay orders without an expedited full hearing, showing of irreparable injury or likelihood of success, a protective bond, and written federal assurance of continued FFP for federally funded programs.

headings.title: Circuit court appeal under section 536.050
headings.reviewNote: Grants recipients or providers the right to appeal from the AHC to the circuit court of Cole County or the county of residence pursuant to section 536.050.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes medical assistance payments for inpatient psychiatric hospital services for individuals under age twenty-one and for nursing home services for recipients of any age except as provided in Title XIX.

headings.title: Inpatient psychiatric hospital services for children
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes agreements for inpatient psychiatric treatment for eligible children under twenty-one years of age.

headings.title: Nursing home services for recipients of any age
headings.reviewNote: Permits medical assistance payments for nursing home services for recipients of any age, except as otherwise provided in Title XIX (42 U.S.C. 1396d).

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates MO HealthNet fraud, provider abuse, recipient overutilization, and mandatory exclusion of abortion facilities.

headings.title: Definitions of provider fraud, abuse, and excessive use
headings.reviewNote: Defines statutory terms including provider abuse, medical assistance fraud, and recipient excessive use.

headings.title: Contract suspension, revocation, or refusal for abuse or fraud
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DSS or its divisions to suspend, revoke, cancel, or refuse a provider contract or agreement upon determining the provider or its staff committed abuse or fraud.

headings.title: Authority to impose prior authorization requirements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DSS or its divisions to impose prior authorization upon reasonable cause to believe abuse, fraud, or excessive use occurred, or by rule for specified services.

headings.title: Confidentiality of abuse, fraud, and excessive use reports
headings.reviewNote: Makes provider or recipient reports of suspected abuse, fraud, or excessive use confidential and bars divulging the reporter's name except in judicial proceedings under protective order.

headings.title: Withholding of provider payments during fraud investigations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes withholding program payments from providers during active fraud and abuse investigations.

headings.title: Identification of recipient excessive service utilization
headings.reviewNote: Directs review of recipient claims to detect pattern overutilization of medical services and prescriptions.

headings.title: Lock-in program restricting recipient provider choice
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to restrict recipients committing excessive use to designated primary providers.

headings.title: Termination of benefits for lock-in program violations
headings.reviewNote: Permits termination of benefits for recipients seeking services outside authorized lock-in providers.

headings.title: Provider sanctions and good-faith immunity for lock-in violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sanctioning or terminating providers who knowingly allow or fail to report subsection 7 lock-in violations, and grants civil immunity for good-faith reports.

headings.title: Mandatory exclusion of convicted providers and abortion facilities
headings.reviewNote: Mandates exclusion of providers convicted of healthcare crimes and abortion facilities or their affiliates.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes managed care, prepaid health plans, and primary care case management for MO HealthNet recipients.

headings.title: Definitions for managed care and prepaid health plans
headings.reviewNote: Defines terms including prepaid capitated payment, primary care case management, and physician sponsor.

headings.title: Duty to maximize cost-effective managed healthcare delivery
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to utilize prepaid health plans and managed care systems to lower program costs.

headings.title: Department authority to contract with prepaid health plans
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes direct contracts with health maintenance organizations and clinic networks for comprehensive care.

headings.title: Recipient freedom of plan selection and overutilization exception
headings.reviewNote: Preserves recipient freedom to select among contracted prepaid or case-management plans and physician sponsors, except in instances of recipient Medicaid overutilization.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes medical assistance payments beginning July 1, 1983 for adult day care and treatment for persons who would otherwise require intermediate care or skilled nursing placement, reimbursed on a reasonable cost basis.

headings.title: Adult day care benefit payments for nursing-eligible persons
headings.reviewNote: Permits medical assistance payments beginning July 1, 1983 for adult day care and treatment for eligible needy persons who would otherwise require intermediate care or skilled nursing home placement.

headings.title: Reasonable cost basis for adult day care payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires payments under this section to be made on the basis of reasonable cost as defined and determined by the MO HealthNet division.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes nursing care reimbursement rate rules (including change-of-ownership freeze, new facility rates, capital formulas, and FY 1996+ negotiated trend factors capped at the HCFA market basket index), with subdivisions 1(1)-(4) expired July 1, 1989.

headings.title: Nursing care rate freeze, new facility capital rules, and trend factor
headings.reviewNote: Sets change-of-ownership rate freeze, new facility operating and capital formulas (subdivisions 1-4, expired July 1, 1989), and FY 1996+ negotiated annual trend factors capped at the HCFA market basket index.

headings.title: July 1, 1989 expiration of subdivisions 1(1) through 1(4)
headings.reviewNote: Provides that subdivisions (1), (2), (3), and (4) of subsection 1 remain in effect only until July 1, 1989 unless otherwise provided by law; source note confirms expiration on July 1, 1989.

entries.reviewSummary: Designates the state treasurer as custodian of department funds and establishes seven special funds separate from general public moneys for supplemental payments, AFDC, calamity relief, child welfare, administration, Title XIX, and child support enforcement.

headings.title: State treasurer custody and disbursement of department funds
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state treasurer as treasurer and custodian of all department funds and requires issuing checks under department rules.

headings.title: Creation of seven special departmental funds
headings.reviewNote: Establishes seven separate special funds: supplemental payment, AFDC, relief, child welfare service, administration, Title XIX, and child support enforcement funds.

headings.title: Supplemental payment fund sources and disbursements
headings.reviewNote: Comprises state appropriations and federal or other moneys for supplemental payments, from which all supplemental payment checks are drawn.

headings.title: Aid to families with dependent children fund
headings.reviewNote: Comprises state appropriations and federal or other moneys for AFDC payments, from which all AFDC checks are drawn.

headings.title: Relief fund for public calamity assistance
headings.reviewNote: Comprises state appropriations and federal or other moneys for aid or relief in cases of public calamity, paying all such expenditures.

headings.title: Child welfare service fund and administration transfer
headings.reviewNote: Comprises state appropriations and federal or other moneys for child welfare services, permitting transfer of all or part to the administration fund.

headings.title: Administration fund for departmental operating and payroll costs
headings.reviewNote: Comprises state appropriations and federal administrative moneys, from which all department employee and personal service checks are drawn.

headings.title: Title XIX fund for medical assistance payments
headings.reviewNote: Comprises state appropriations and federal or other moneys for Title XIX state plan medical assistance, from which all recipient-behalf checks are drawn.

headings.title: Child support enforcement fund collections and disbursements
