headings.reviewNote: Comprises state, federal, assigned support, fee, and incentive moneys used to pay returned obligations, local and interstate incentives, federal AFDC reimbursements, and child support administrative costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs the DSS director to apply for an amended federal comparability-of-services waiver to extend institutional-status medical assistance to at-risk home and community-based care individuals subject to appropriations and section 536.024 rulemaking.

headings.title: Application for amended federal waiver of comparability of services
headings.reviewNote: Requires the DSS director within thirty days of August 28, 1992 to apply to HHS for an amended 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(10)(A)(ii)(VI) comparability waiver covering 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5 individuals.

headings.title: Rules extending institutional status to home and community-based care
headings.reviewNote: Requires the DSS director upon receiving the amended waiver, subject to appropriations, to promulgate rules applying institutional status to individuals at risk of nursing placement who can be cared for at home.

headings.title: Section 536.024 rulemaking effectiveness requirement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no rule or portion of a rule promulgated under this chapter becomes effective unless promulgated pursuant to section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the thirteen-member Drug Utilization Review Board within MO HealthNet, defines member expertise, quarterly meetings, staggered terms, expense-only service, practitioner outreach, OBRA 1990 monitoring, Missouri Rx advice, division support, and up to six regional advisory committees.

headings.title: Establishment and thirteen-member composition of DUR Board
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Drug Utilization Review Board within the MO HealthNet division with six physicians, six pharmacists, and one certified medical quality assurance RN appointed by the governor with senate consent.

headings.title: Required clinical and quality assurance expertise
headings.reviewNote: Requires board members to have recognized expertise in outpatient drug prescribing, dispensing and monitoring, drug use review and intervention, or medical quality assurance.

headings.title: Chairperson election, quarterly meetings, and eight-member quorum
headings.reviewNote: Requires electing a chairperson, meeting at least once every ninety days, and an eight-member quorum including at least three physicians and three pharmacists.

headings.title: Four-year terms, staggered initial terms, and reappointment
headings.reviewNote: Sets four-year terms with staggered two-, three-, and four-year initial appointments and permits member reappointment.

headings.title: Uncompensated service with reasonable expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that DUR Board and regional advisory committee members receive no compensation other than reasonable actual expenses incurred in official duties.

headings.title: Practitioner educational outreach on drug therapy problems
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board, directly or via division contracts with educational institutions or professional societies, to provide educational outreach improving prescribing and dispensing practices.

headings.title: OBRA 1990 Medicaid drug utilization monitoring and newsletter
headings.reviewNote: Requires monitoring Medicaid drug usage under OBRA 1990 Section 4401(g), publishing a provider formulary newsletter, and advising providers of inappropriate utilization.

headings.title: Advisory role for Missouri Rx plan guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Permits the Drug Utilization Review Board to provide advice on guidelines, policies, and procedures for the Missouri Rx plan.

headings.title: MO HealthNet division office space and staff support
headings.reviewNote: Requires the MO HealthNet division to provide office space and support personnel for the board.

headings.title: Regional advisory committees of physicians and pharmacists
headings.reviewNote: Permits appointing up to six regional advisory committees of physicians and pharmacists with specified drug-use expertise, subject to specific appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires monthly advance benefit payments directly to recipients, conservators, or caretaker relatives with direct institutional payments and fee-free incapacity proceedings, permits third-party protective payments for dependent children, and allows probate court orders for next of kin or creditors to collect deceased recipients' uncashed checks.

headings.title: Monthly advance payments, direct institutional pay, and fee-free probate
headings.reviewNote: Requires monthly advance payments to recipients, conservators, or relatives (allowing post-care direct hospital or nursing home payments) and waives fees in probate incapacity proceedings for indigent recipients.

headings.title: Third-party protective payments for dependent children
headings.reviewNote: Permits paying dependent child benefits to a third party or vendor when the caretaker relative cannot manage funds in the child's best interest or refuses section 208.042 work programs.

headings.title: Probate order to endorse deceased recipient's uncashed benefit check
headings.reviewNote: Permits a fee-free probate court order upon next-of-kin or creditor affidavit authorizing endorsement and collection of a deceased recipient's uncashed check for funeral expenses and debts when no estate administration is required.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires EBT pilot projects in St. Louis City and counties of 600,000+, prohibits vendor disclosure of EBT data as a class A misdemeanor, mandates photo ID EBT cards subject to appropriations and waivers, requires rulemaking, and consolidates multiple benefit programs onto one card.

headings.title: Electronic benefit transfer pilot projects in St. Louis City and large counties
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to establish EBT pilot projects in St. Louis City and counties of 600,000+ allowing ATM or point-of-sale cash withdrawals with account status receipts.

headings.title: Prohibition on vendor data disclosure and class A misdemeanor
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits financial institutions, businesses, or vendors from using, selling, or divulging FSD-provided information without a court order, classifying violations as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Photographic identification requirement on EBT cards
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS, subject to appropriations and federal waivers, to use photographic identification on approved EBT cards.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking for EBT system implementation
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to promulgate necessary implementation rules pursuant to section 660.017 and chapter 536.

headings.title: Single-card consolidation of multiple benefit programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires electronic benefit delivery and eligibility verification for AFDC, WIC, EPSDT, food stamps, SSI/Medicaid, child support, and other programs to reside in one multi-function card.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Advisory Council on Rare Diseases and Personalized Medicine within MO HealthNet to advise the DUR Board on orphan drugs and personalized medicine, sets member composition, meetings, consultation topics, public written recommendations, rare disease definition, and annual conflict-of-interest disclosures.

headings.title: Establishment of Advisory Council on Rare Diseases and Personalized Medicine
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the advisory council within MO HealthNet to consult with the DUR Board on beneficiary access to rare disease drugs and biological products and defines beneficiary access.

headings.title: Appointment and composition of advisory council members
headings.reviewNote: Directs the DSS director to appoint medical school physicians, researchers, nurses, pharmacists, patient and foundation representatives, a pediatric rare disease center member, and ex officio chairs; source notes record 'chair'/'chair's' in H.B. 1953.

headings.title: Initial meeting deadline and subsequent meeting calls
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to convene the first meeting by February 28, 2019, with subsequent meetings called by the DUR Board chair or a majority of council members.

headings.title: Mandatory DUR Board consultation on rare disease and personalized therapies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the DUR Board to request and consider council information when addressing access to federal Orphan Drug Act rare disease therapies, personalized medicine, and noninheritable gene-editing therapeutics.

headings.title: Consultation topics for rare disease policy review
headings.reviewNote: Directs the DUR Board to seek council input on eight topics including disease severity, unmet need, Medicaid policy impacts on access and adherence, benefit-risk assessment, specialist access, and patient demographics.

headings.title: No legal right to consultation or specific stakeholder meetings
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies this section creates no legal right to a consultation on any matter and does not require the DUR Board to meet with any particular expert or stakeholder.

headings.title: Written explanation of recommendations at public hearings
headings.reviewNote: Requires council recommendations on rare disease treatments to be explained in writing to DUR Board members during public hearings.

headings.title: Definition of rare disease drug
headings.reviewNote: Defines rare disease drug as a drug treating a rare medical condition affecting fewer than 200,000 persons in the United States, such as cystic fibrosis, hemophilia, and multiple myeloma.

headings.title: Annual conflict of interest disclosures and twenty-percent conflict-free rule
headings.reviewNote: Requires all council members to annually sign conflict-of-interest statements and requires at least twenty percent of members to have no conflict with insurers, PBMs, or pharmaceutical manufacturers.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires the Advisory Council on Rare Diseases and Personalized Medicine to annually review MO HealthNet coverage, promising late-stage treatments, and minority provider education for sickle cell disease, and permits public division reports or posted expert input.

headings.title: Annual advisory council review of sickle cell disease care
headings.reviewNote: Requires the advisory council at least once each calendar year to evaluate MO HealthNet coverage adequacy for sickle cell disease, review promising late-stage treatments, and review provider education on minority impacts.

headings.title: Optional public report and website posting of expert input
headings.reviewNote: Permits MO HealthNet division staff, under council guidance, to develop a public report or compile and post solicited expert testimony or input on the division website.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the MO HealthNet Division within DSS, governs director appointment, type I transfer of medical assistance administration from FSD, continuation of prior rules, chapter 36 staffing, and ten enumerated division powers.

headings.title: Establishment of MO HealthNet Division and director appointment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the MO HealthNet Division within DSS with a director appointed by the DSS director and equates statutory references to division of medical services with MO HealthNet division.

headings.title: Division status and provider payment administration
headings.reviewNote: Designates the MO HealthNet Division as an integral part of DSS exercising necessary statutory powers and administering MO HealthNet provider payments.

headings.title: Type I transfer from FSD and retained eligibility authority
headings.reviewNote: Transfers medical assistance administration powers from FSD to the MO HealthNet Division by type I transfer while FSD retains authority to determine and regulate MO HealthNet eligibility.

headings.title: Continuation of existing division of medical services rules
headings.reviewNote: Keeps all state regulations adopted under the division of medical services in effect unless withdrawn or amended by the MO HealthNet Division.

headings.title: Chapter 36 appointing authority and division subdivisions
headings.reviewNote: Grants the MO HealthNet Division director chapter 36 appointing authority to employ necessary personnel and permits designating subdivisions.

headings.title: Enumerated powers of the MO HealthNet Division
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates ten division powers including suing, rulemaking, contracting, administering funds, federal cooperation and reporting, advisory committees, payment policies, utilization reviews, and research or demonstration projects.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes MO HealthNet to administer medical funds for children in DSS custody, requires identifying children in state custody solely for mental health needs, mandates sixty-day court-approved individualized service plans, and governs DMH-to-DSS billing upon family return.

headings.title: MO HealthNet administration of medical funds for children in custody
headings.reviewNote: Permits the MO HealthNet Division to administer DSS-appropriated funds for paying medical care of children in DSS or division legal custody.

headings.title: Identification of children in custody solely for mental health needs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the children's division through judicial review or family support team meetings to identify cases in the system exclusively for mental health services with no abuse, neglect, or abandonment.

headings.title: Sixty-day individualized service plan and court approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicable agencies within sixty days to develop a family-involved, least-restrictive individualized service plan identifying payers and providers for judicial approval and potential return to family custody.

headings.title: Department of Mental Health billing under joint financing plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires DMH to bill DSS for care costs under a jointly developed comprehensive financing plan when children return to family custody and become DMH service responsibility.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires public assistance recipients and living spouses to report undeclared excess income or property to FSD, authorizes recovery of improperly paid benefits without interest as a state debt, sets a prima facie ownership presumption, and allocates federal recovery shares.

headings.title: Duty to report undeclared excess property or income
headings.reviewNote: Requires recipients or living spouses possessing undeclared property or income affecting need or eligibility to notify FSD, which may cancel or alter benefits after investigation.

headings.title: Recovery of overpaid or misrepresented benefits as state debt
headings.reviewNote: Makes benefits paid during undeclared property or income possession, or obtained through misrepresentation, nondisclosure, or mistake of fact, recoverable without interest from the recipient or estate as a state debt.

headings.title: Prima facie presumption of ownership during benefit period
headings.reviewNote: Makes possession of undeclared property by a recipient or living spouse prima facie evidence of ownership during benefit receipt, placing the burden of proof otherwise on the recipient or legal representative.

headings.title: Federal government share of recovered amounts
headings.reviewNote: Entitles the federal government to share in collections up to its contribution in each case, requiring prompt DSS payment or credit to the designated federal agency.

entries.reviewSummary: Excludes qualifying actuarially sound annuities naming Missouri as contingent beneficiary from MO HealthNet available resources, sets a sixty-month look-back period for annuity investments, and mandates chapter 536 rulemaking.

headings.title: Resource exclusion criteria for qualifying annuities
headings.reviewNote: Excludes income streams from annuities that are actuarially sound under SSA life tables, pay equal non-balloon installments, name Missouri as contingent beneficiary up to MO HealthNet expenditures, and pay the claimant primarily.

headings.title: Sixty-month look-back period and pre-August 28, 2005 rule
headings.reviewNote: Requires a sixty-month look-back period for annuity investments made to obtain MO HealthNet eligibility with full federal and state remedies, without automatically disallowing pre-August 28, 2005 annuities.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate administration rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2005.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets six conditions for a personal care contract to constitute fair and valuable consideration in institutionalized Medicaid eligibility determinations under 42 U.S.C. 1396p and bases fair market value on county provider rates.

headings.title: Six criteria for personal care contracts as fair consideration
headings.reviewNote: Requires a prior signed written agreement specifying services, no duplication, documented need, essentialness to avoid institutionalization, payment within two months, and equal pre-institutionalization fair market value under 42 U.S.C. 1396p.

headings.title: County provider rate basis for fair market value
headings.reviewNote: Bases the fair market value of personal care services on the current rate paid to providers of such services in the county of residence.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes MO HealthNet as payer of last resort with subrogation, direct recovery actions, mandatory notice and assignment, third-party liens, judicial lien adjudication and fee sharing, TEFRA real property liens, 30-day injury reporting, medical support liability, and compromise authority.

headings.title: Payer of last resort status and subrogation claim processing
headings.reviewNote: Declares MO HealthNet payer of last resort, makes third-party payments a state debt, and requires health plans, TPAs, ASOs, and PBMs to process subrogation claims for three years with six-year enforcement and Medicare carve-outs.

headings.title: State action to recover MO HealthNet funds from liable parties
headings.reviewNote: Permits DSS, MO HealthNet division, or its contractor to maintain an action in the state's name against any party liable to a participant, minor, or estate.

headings.title: Participant and wrongful death claimant notice of legal pursuit
headings.reviewNote: Requires participants, guardians, estates, and section 537.080 wrongful death claimants with actual knowledge of MO HealthNet payments to promptly notify MO HealthNet when pursuing liable third parties.

headings.title: Assignment of recovery rights, cooperation, and sixty-day payment
headings.reviewNote: Assigns recovery rights by application, requires third-party cooperation on pain of ineligibility, and requires paying MO HealthNet or placing funds in trust within sixty days of receiving settlement proceeds.

headings.title: Representative notice of claim pursuit and thirty-day settlement notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires representatives pursuing nonwork-related claims for MO HealthNet-eligible persons to notify MO HealthNet upon engagement, filing, or settlement and give thirty days' notice before satisfying any judgment or settlement.

headings.title: Prompt recovery notice and immediate reimbursement duty
headings.reviewNote: Requires participants, representatives, estates, and attorneys to promptly notify MO HealthNet of third-party recoveries and immediately reimburse DSS, barring satisfaction without notice and opportunity to assert the claim.

headings.title: Right of recovery and HIPAA 270/271 eligibility data disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a recovery right against liable third parties and requires third-party payers (excluding accident-only, specified disease, disability income, or fixed indemnity policies) to provide HIPAA 270/271 data.

headings.title: Statutory lien on insurance proceeds, settlements, and attorney funds
headings.reviewNote: Creates a DSS/MO HealthNet lien on settlement, judgment, or attorney-held funds upon certified or registered mail service of lien notice on liable parties.

headings.title: Judicial adjudication of lien rights and six evidentiary factors
headings.reviewNote: Permits court adjudication of lien rights and approval of settlements after an evidentiary hearing considering six factors including lien percentage, fees and costs, medical expenses, full recompense, future needs, and ability to pay.

headings.title: Burden of proof for reduction and prima facie computerized records
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of producing evidence for a lien reduction on the requesting party and makes certified MO HealthNet computerized records prima facie evidence of state expenditures and debt.

headings.title: Lien apportionment, pro rata attorney fees, and lien priority
headings.reviewNote: Permits proportional lien reduction, requires MO HealthNet to pay its pro rata share of attorney fees, preserves section 484.140 attorney lien priority, and gives state charges priority over all other state liens.

headings.title: Satisfaction of attorney fees first and director compromise authority
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits satisfying a state charge before attorney fee claims are satisfied and preserves the director's authority to compromise claims after considering subsections 9 to 13.

headings.title: Workers' compensation exclusion, federal share, and TEFRA liens
headings.reviewNote: Excludes chapter 287 workers' compensation claims, allocates federal recovery shares, and governs recording, pre-death limits, family-residence exemptions, and dissolution of 42 U.S.C. 1396p TEFRA real property liens.

headings.title: Subordination to attorney liens and claim expenses
headings.reviewNote: Subordinates the state debt under this section to section 484.130 or 484.140 attorney liens and participant third-party claim expenses.

headings.title: Assignment of medical support and payment rights
headings.reviewNote: Makes application for and acceptance of MO HealthNet benefits an assignment to DSS or MO HealthNet of court- or administratively-ordered medical support and other medical payment rights.

headings.title: Thirty-day participant duty to report personal injuries
headings.reviewNote: Requires all chapter 208 benefit participants to report personal injuries to themselves or MO HealthNet household members to FSD or MO HealthNet within thirty days.

headings.title: State recovery from persons failing medical support obligations
headings.reviewNote: Makes persons who violate court or administrative medical insurance orders or owe a duty of support liable to the state for the entire cost of public assistance medical care provided to the dependent child, spouse, or ex-spouse.

headings.title: Compromise, waiver, and cost-effectiveness exception for pursuit
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to compromise, settle, or waive claims and relieves MO HealthNet from pursuing third parties when expected recovery is less than cost or not cost-effective under three criteria.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires DSS to pay attorney fees (capped at 25% of annual maximum SSI grant) for attorneys winning favorable ALJ federal SSI appeals for general relief recipients upon petition within sixty days, and mandates rulemaking.

headings.title: Department payment of attorney fees for favorable SSI appeals
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to pay attorneys winning favorable ALJ federal SSI appeals for general relief recipients up to 25% of the annual max individual SSI grant within thirty days of a petition filed within sixty days of the decision.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking for SSI appeal fee disbursements
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate necessary implementation rules pursuant to section 208.151 and chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes DSS and DMH to contract with insurers, HMOs, TPAs, ASOs, and PBMs for medical insurance data matches, limits disclosures to MO HealthNet-covered benefits, sets cost reimbursement, 60-day HIPAA compliance with $10/day penalties, class A misdemeanor privacy rules, and deemed participant consent.

headings.title: Definitions for medical insurance data matching
headings.reviewNote: Defines data match, department, entity (insurers, HMOs, self-insureds, TPAs, ASOs, PBMs), individual, insurance, and request.

headings.title: Insurer obligation to provide recipient coverage details
headings.reviewNote: Requires health insurers to supply coverage, identity, and policy data upon department request.

headings.title: Limitation of disclosures to MO HealthNet-covered benefits
headings.reviewNote: Limits required entity disclosures to insurance benefits claimable and payable for medical services or items otherwise covered under MO HealthNet.

headings.title: Data match identification format and biannual request frequency
headings.reviewNote: Requires compatible person-identifying data match requests pertaining to individuals or legally responsible persons, permitted at least twice per year.

headings.title: Reimbursement of entity actual direct data match costs
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to reimburse actual direct industry-standard costs for contract data matches and specify delivery terms, with no reimbursement for non-data-match requests.

headings.title: Sixty-day HIPAA compliance, civil penalties, and ANSI eligibility transactions
headings.reviewNote: Requires HIPAA-compliant responses within sixty days (with up to $10/day civil penalties enforceable by the attorney general for willful failure) and requires carriers and TPAs to handle HIPAA ANSI eligibility transactions.

headings.title: Confidentiality guidelines and class A misdemeanor penalty
headings.reviewNote: Requires the DSS director to set privacy guidelines for exchanged data and makes unauthorized disclosure of confidential information a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Deemed participant consent to insurance inquiries
headings.reviewNote: Deems application for or receipt of sections 208.151 to 208.159 benefits as consent allowing DSS to request insurance coverage information from any entity.

headings.title: Applicability to Department of Mental Health
headings.reviewNote: Applies all DSS provisions of this section to the Department of Mental Health when contracting with entities regarding DMH service recipients.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes fingerprint-based criminal history background checks for MO HealthNet provider enrollment applicants.

headings.title: Fingerprint submission requirement for provider applicants
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the Medicaid audit and compliance unit to require fingerprints from provider enrollment applicants.

headings.title: Submission of fingerprints to State Highway Patrol
headings.reviewNote: Directs applicants to submit fingerprints to the highway patrol for state and federal background checks.

headings.title: Central repository record search and FBI check
headings.reviewNote: Provides for searching state records and forwarding prints to the FBI, with results shared with the compliance unit.

headings.title: Definitions of MO HealthNet provider and services
headings.reviewNote: Defines MO HealthNet provider and MO HealthNet services for criminal background check purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs Medicaid per diem reimbursement rate recalculations and capital expenditure adjustments for nursing homes.

headings.title: Nursing home Medicaid per diem rate recalculation
headings.reviewNote: Directs the MO HealthNet division to recalculate nursing home per diem reimbursement rates using cost reports.

headings.title: Cost report baselines and cost center class ceilings
headings.reviewNote: Establishes formula redetermining patient care, ancillary, and administrative median class ceilings.

headings.title: Rate recalculation for qualifying capital expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes per diem rate adjustments for nursing facilities incurring capital expenditures exceeding two thousand dollars per bed.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits restrictions precluding access to antipsychotic medications in MO HealthNet and provides clinical edits.

headings.title: Prohibition on access restrictions for antipsychotics
headings.reviewNote: Bars imposing access restrictions that preclude the availability of any individual antipsychotic drug.

headings.title: Permitted clinical edits for patient safety
headings.reviewNote: Allows clinical edits for drug safety, polypharmacy detection, and adherence to medical association guidelines.

headings.title: Biannual provider updates on antipsychotic therapy
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to publish biannual provider updates outlining evidence-based psychiatric treatment standards.

headings.title: Grandfathering participant access to stable medications
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees continuing participant access to antipsychotic medications on which they are currently stable.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes pharmaceutical case management, polypharmacy review, and opioid surveillance programs.

headings.title: Polypharmacy case management and opioid surveillance
headings.reviewNote: Directs establishment of case management and opioid surveillance programs for high-risk participants.

headings.title: Authorized clinical edits and best practice guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Permits clinical edits verifying drug safety and preventing adverse drug interactions.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and severability provisions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative regulations under chapter 536 subject to nonseverability conditions.

headings.title: Federal waivers and state plan amendment submissions
headings.reviewNote: Requires submission of state plan amendments or waivers to implement pharmacy management initiatives.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires pharmaceutical manufacturers to pay federal best-price and inflation-adjusted rebates under 42 U.S.C. 1396r-8 on covered outpatient drugs dispensed to MO HealthNet participants and incorporates 42 CFR 447.502 drug definitions.

headings.title: Manufacturer best-price and inflation rebates on outpatient drugs
headings.reviewNote: Requires pharmaceutical manufacturers under 42 U.S.C. 1396r-8 to pay best-price rebates for single source and innovator multiple source drugs and inflation-excess rebates for all covered MO HealthNet outpatient drugs.

headings.title: Incorporation of federal outpatient drug definitions
headings.reviewNote: Incorporates the definitions of innovator multiple source drug, noninnovator multiple source drug, and single source drug from 42 CFR 447.502.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Public Assistance Beneficiary Employer Disclosure Act, directing DSS to publish the quarterly public Missouri Health Care Responsibility Report detailing MO HealthNet enrollment and state costs for employers with fifty or more beneficiary employees.

headings.title: Short title of Public Assistance Beneficiary Employer Disclosure Act
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section shall be known and may be cited as the Public Assistance Beneficiary Employer Disclosure Act.

headings.title: Quarterly Missouri Health Care Responsibility Report and data sources
headings.reviewNote: Directs DSS to submit a quarterly MO HealthNet beneficiary employer report to the governor, defines MO HealthNet beneficiary, and authorizes gathering data from applications, insurance vendors, and voluntary employer submissions.

headings.title: Required employer workforce, insurance, and state cost disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Specifies ten data categories for employers with 50+ MO HealthNet beneficiary employees or spouses/custodial parents, including Title XIX/XXI percentages, full/part-time status, employer coverage, total and per capita state costs, and industry categories.

headings.title: Proportional counting of beneficiaries with multiple employers
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to count a MO HealthNet beneficiary having more than one employer as a portion of one person for each employer.

headings.title: Quarterly publication schedule and public availability
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing the report 120 days after each calendar quarter starting Q1 2008 on the DSS website, with public right to request printed copies.

entries.reviewSummary: Suspends the federal SNAP work requirement waiver from January 1, 2016 through January 1, 2019, dedicates resulting state savings to child care, education, transportation, and job training subject to appropriations, and mandates annual legislative reports; source note records 2015 S.B. 24 veto override.

headings.title: Inapplicability of SNAP work requirement waiver until 2019
headings.reviewNote: Provides that beginning January 1, 2016 the 7 U.S.C. 2015(o) SNAP work requirement waiver shall not apply in Missouri, terminating January 1, 2019.

headings.title: Use of state savings for child care, education, and job training
headings.reviewNote: Directs ongoing state expenditure savings from SNAP and TANF modifications, subject to appropriations, to child care for single-parent households, education, transportation, and job training.

headings.title: Annual report to Joint Committee on Government Accountability
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual DSS report on sections 208.026 and 208.040 implementation and requires the joint committee to meet annually and make recommendations to legislative leaders.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts qualifying individuals with controlled substance possession or use felony convictions from the federal food stamp ban upon treatment, compliance, and self-paid sobriety testing, requires satisfactory evidence and rulemaking, and excludes individuals with two subsequent drug felonies; source note records 2014 S.B. 727 veto override.

headings.title: Exemption from federal drug-felony food stamp ban
headings.reviewNote: Exempts individuals convicted of controlled substance possession or use felonies from the 21 U.S.C. 862a(a) food stamp ban if meeting substance abuse treatment, court/probation compliance, one-year offense-free, and self-paid urinalysis criteria.

headings.title: Documentary evidence and general eligibility requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires subsection 1 eligibility to be supported by documentary or other evidence satisfactory to DSS and requires meeting all other food stamp eligibility factors.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking on treatment participation criteria
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS, in consultation with the division of alcohol and drug abuse, to promulgate implementation rules specifying active treatment participation and completion criteria.

headings.title: Inapplicability after two subsequent controlled substance felonies
headings.reviewNote: Excludes individuals convicted of or pleading guilty or nolo contendere to two subsequent controlled substance possession or use felonies after their first drug felony conviction.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Food is Medicine Act, defines medically tailored groceries, meals, and produce prescriptions, authorizes a CMS Section 1115 waiver for MO HealthNet nutrition services prioritizing community organizations and local growers, and mandates chapter 536 rulemaking.

headings.title: Short title of Food is Medicine Act
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section shall be known and may be cited as the Food is Medicine Act.

headings.title: Definitions of medically tailored groceries, meals, and produce prescriptions
headings.reviewNote: Defines medically tailored groceries, medically tailored meals, and produce prescriptions prescribed by registered dietitians, licensed physicians, or qualified clinical teams.

headings.title: Section 1115 demonstration waiver for Food is Medicine program
headings.reviewNote: Permits DSS to apply to CMS for a Section 1115 demonstration waiver to provide MO HealthNet nutritional support improving health outcomes for nutrition-related chronic diseases.

headings.title: Permitted covered nutrition services
headings.reviewNote: Lists nutrition services that may be covered, including case management, nutrition counseling, and prescribed medically tailored groceries, medically tailored meals, and produce prescriptions.

headings.title: Priority for community organizations and local growers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the MO HealthNet division, whenever feasible, to prioritize community-based organizations and local growers to support locally grown food in nutrition prescriptions.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate administration rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2026.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs the Department of Agriculture to apply for USDA Senior and WIC Farmers' Market Nutrition Program grants, establishes the Missouri Farmers' Market Nutrition Program providing produce vouchers or electronic cards to eligible seniors 60+ and WIC participants, mandates interagency cooperation, and authorizes rulemaking.

headings.title: USDA Senior and WIC Farmers' Market Nutrition Program grant applications
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Department of Agriculture to apply for USDA Senior and WIC Farmers' Market Nutrition Program grants to provide vouchers or electronic cards for eligible foods at farmers' markets.

headings.title: Establishment and purpose of Missouri Farmers' Market Nutrition Program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the program within the Department of Agriculture to supply Missouri-grown fresh produce via vouchers or approved payments at designated Missouri farmers' markets.

headings.title: Voucher distribution sites and participating market lists
headings.reviewNote: Directs eligible seniors and nutritionally at-risk WIC women, infants, and children under five to receive vouchers at county or neighboring distribution sites with lists of participating farmers and markets.

headings.title: Definition of eligible program participant
headings.reviewNote: Defines participant as a person age 60+ meeting annual USDA income guidelines or a participant in the DHSS WIC special supplemental nutrition program.

headings.title: Interagency and nonprofit cooperation agreements
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Department of Agriculture and participating state, local, or nonprofit entities to cooperate, including entering written agreements to maintain the USDA programs.

headings.title: Permissive rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department to promulgate implementation rules subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 nonseverability for rules after August 28, 2018.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Family Self-Sufficiency Program, pacts, case management, asset allowances, and sanctions.

headings.title: Enrollment of AFDC recipients in self-sufficiency program
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to enroll assistance recipients into the family self-sufficiency program.

headings.title: Target enrollment quotas and priority household categories
headings.reviewNote: Sets statutory quotas and target categories for enrolling households into self-sufficiency pacts.

headings.title: Initial assessment of family education and employment needs
headings.reviewNote: Requires comprehensive initial evaluations of participant educational, employment, and support needs.

headings.title: Development of customized family self-sufficiency pact
headings.reviewNote: Mandates negotiation of a written self-sufficiency pact establishing specific goals and completion milestones.

headings.title: Division assessment duties and agency contracting
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division caseworkers or contracted agencies to conduct pact assessments and case planning.

headings.title: Pact development conferences and required participants
headings.reviewNote: Specifies attendees for pact planning conferences including caseworkers, job specialists, and participants.

headings.title: Mutual contractual obligations and supportive service terms
headings.reviewNote: Establishes mutual commitments regarding child care, job training, education, and employment search.

headings.title: Parent and child development plan components
headings.reviewNote: Includes parenting skills, child health, and educational development goals within the family pact.

headings.title: Enhanced resource limits for enrolled families
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes enrolled households to retain up to five thousand dollars in personal assets and savings.

headings.title: Automobile ownership exemption from resource limits
headings.reviewNote: Exempts one motor vehicle per household from public assistance property limitations.

headings.title: Earned income disregards for employment transitions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes disregards of up to two-thirds of gross earned income to promote work transitions.

headings.title: Administrative review rights for contested pact provisions
headings.reviewNote: Allows recipients to request division director review of disputed self-sufficiency pact terms.

headings.title: Extension and modification of pact terms for barrier removal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes pact deadline extensions when significant employment barriers or service shortages arise.

headings.title: Service capacity shortages and substitution allowances
headings.reviewNote: Permits service substitutions and timeline adjustments when required community services are unavailable.

headings.title: Case manager training programs and professional competencies
headings.reviewNote: Establishes training curricula for case managers covering public programs, job markets, and counseling.

headings.title: Promotion of federal earned income tax credit utilization
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to assist participating families in applying for the federal earned income tax credit.

headings.title: Recalculation of cash grants for noncompliance with pacts
headings.reviewNote: Provides progressive grant reductions and caretaker benefit suspensions for unexcused pact noncompliance.

headings.title: Review procedures for caretaker benefit suspensions
headings.reviewNote: Grants participants the right to director review prior to implementing caretaker sanction suspensions.

headings.title: Reapplication rules following program completion and limits
headings.reviewNote: Governs subsequent assistance eligibility for recipients who previously completed thirty-six months of aid.

headings.title: Independent comprehensive evaluation of program outcomes
headings.reviewNote: Requires an independent empirical study evaluating employment outcomes, wage gains, and welfare dependency.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority for self-sufficiency pacts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative regulations governing self-sufficiency programs under chapter 536.

headings.title: Application for necessary federal statutory waivers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department director to seek all necessary federal waivers from the Department of Health and Human Services.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes FSD to deposit state-entitled child support into accounts for children whose custodial parents are in JOBS/FUTURES and noncustodial parents are in job training, requires mutual parental expenditure approval, state treasurer deposits with earnings, annual statements, and federal HHS waivers before implementation.

headings.title: Deposits into child accounts for JOBS/FUTURES and training parents
headings.reviewNote: Permits FSD to deposit up to the state-entitled portion of current child support into accounts for children whose custodial parent participates in sections 208.400 to 208.425 and noncustodial parent participates in approved job training or education.

headings.title: Account naming, joint parental expenditure approval, and rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires accounting in the child's name, limits expenditures to child care or services agreed upon by both parents, and mandates FSD rules under section 454.400 and chapter 536.

headings.title: State treasurer deposit and crediting of account earnings
headings.reviewNote: Requires FSD to deposit appropriated moneys with the state treasurer and credit attributable earnings to each child's account.

headings.title: Annual transaction statements for children and parents
headings.reviewNote: Requires the DSS division of finance and administrative services to furnish each child and parents an annual statement listing all account receipts and disbursements.

headings.title: Mandatory federal HHS waiver prerequisite before implementation
headings.reviewNote: Requires the DSS director to apply for all necessary federal waivers and prohibits implementing the program until the federal HHS Secretary grants the waiver.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires DESE to offer the Postponing Sexual Involvement Program to schools upon request and requires DSS to expand QUEST and offer the Rites of Passage Program to schools upon request.

headings.title: Postponing Sexual Involvement Program for schools
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of elementary and secondary education to offer the Postponing Sexual Involvement Program to all schools upon request.

headings.title: QUEST expansion and Rites of Passage Program
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to establish one additional QUEST location and offer the Rites of Passage Program to all schools upon request.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs the family support division to establish and administer the JOBS program under Title IV-F, mandates fiscal year 1986 state funding maintenance of effort, and requires interagency planning without service duplication.

headings.title: Establishment of JOBS program for AFDC recipients
headings.reviewNote: Requires the family support division to establish a job opportunities and basic skills training (JOBS) program for AFDC recipients by October 1, 1990.

headings.title: Administration of JOBS under Title IV-F
headings.reviewNote: Requires the family support division, subject to appropriation, to administer the JOBS program under Title IV-F of the federal Social Security Act.

headings.title: Maintenance of state funding effort
headings.reviewNote: Requires state funds expended for P.L. 100-485 programs to be no less than the fiscal year 1986 expenditure level.

headings.title: Interagency planning and coordination without duplication
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to plan and coordinate JOBS with the Missouri Job Training Coordinating Council, DESE, DOLIR, and DED without duplicating services.

entries.reviewSummary: Prioritizes volunteers in the JOBS program, requires volunteer recruitment outreach, exempts parents caring for children under age three, mandates pretermination hearings before sanctions, and authorizes sanction rules.

headings.title: Priority participation for volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Requires giving priority to individuals who volunteer to participate under Section 201 of P.L. 100-485.

headings.title: Publicity and recruitment program for volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state plan to include a publicity and recruitment program aimed at serving volunteers first.

headings.title: Exemption for parents caring for children under age three
headings.reviewNote: Exempts AFDC recipients personally caring for a child under age three in the home from required JOBS participation.

headings.title: Pretermination hearing requirement before sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits terminating benefits or supportive services as a JOBS sanction without a prior hearing on the record with an opportunity to present facts and arguments.

headings.title: Refusal of services without good cause and sanction rules
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits refusing JOBS services without good cause and authorizes the division to promulgate sanction rules consistent with the Family Support Act of 1988.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires public assistance recipients who have not completed high school to participate in basic education or GED preparation, subject to federal exemptions and a thirty-six-month voluntary phase-in.

headings.title: Basic education and GED participation requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires AFDC, general relief, and food stamp recipients without a high school diploma or GED to enroll in and attend a basic education or GED program.

headings.title: Exemption criteria under Family Support Act
headings.reviewNote: Applies the exemption criteria of the federal Family Support Act of 1988 to this section.

headings.title: Provision of child care and transportation services
headings.reviewNote: Requires providing necessary child care and transportation services to participants in basic education or GED programs.

headings.title: Thirty-six-month voluntary period and long-term recipient mandate
headings.reviewNote: Makes participation voluntary for thirty-six months after July 27, 1989, after which participation may be required for recipients of AFDC in thirty-six of the preceding sixty months.

entries.reviewSummary: Imposes a reimbursement allowance on Medicaid managed care organizations based on revenues and clarifies treatment as a tax or cost for rate-setting purposes. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.437).

headings.title: Medicaid managed care organization reimbursement allowance
headings.reviewNote: Requires each Medicaid managed care organization to pay a reimbursement allowance based on a formula set by department rule and derived from direct Medicaid revenues.

headings.title: Treatment of allowance as tax or cost for rate setting
headings.reviewNote: Requires treating the reimbursement allowance as a tax or cost in managed care rate setting rather than as a Medicaid managed care organization administrative cost.

headings.title: Allowance calculation formula and federal authorization condition
headings.reviewNote: Establishes formula rules and conditions collection on federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires Medicaid managed care organizations to maintain and report revenue records to the department of social services and protects confidential proprietary data. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.437).

headings.title: Recordkeeping and reporting of managed care revenues
headings.reviewNote: Requires each Medicaid managed care organization to keep revenue records and submit required reports under oath to the department of social services.

headings.title: Confidentiality of proprietary revenue information
headings.reviewNote: Protects proprietary information contained in managed care revenue reports from disclosure as confidential.

headings.title: Offset of reimbursement allowance against state payments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes offset of owed allowances against state Medicaid payments upon managed care plan request.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires the department of social services to determine managed care reimbursement allowance amounts, send final notices, and permit administrative protests and judicial review. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.437).

headings.title: Determination and notice of reimbursement allowance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to determine each managed care organization's allowance, send notice, and treat the determination as final after thirty days unless protested.

headings.title: Protest, hearing, and chapter 536 judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Permits a Medicaid managed care organization to file a written protest within thirty days for a departmental hearing, written decision, and chapter 536 judicial review.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires rulemaking for the managed care reimbursement allowance formula and collection, permits payment offsets against Medicaid capitation payments, and allows allowance recalculations. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.437).

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking for allowance formula and collection
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to promulgate rules establishing the reimbursement allowance formula, notification, and collection procedures.

headings.title: Collection, offset against Medicaid payments, and recalculations
headings.reviewNote: Provides for collecting the allowance via payment or offset against Medicaid payments, permits periodic recalculation by rule, and credits offsets to the reimbursement allowance fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Medicaid Managed Care Organization Reimbursement Allowance Fund, exempts it from general revenue reversion, and accepts fund offsets or payments as satisfying the section 208.431 obligation. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.437).

headings.title: Creation and administration of Medicaid MCO Reimbursement Allowance Fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs remittance to DSS payable to DOR for deposit into the dedicated Medicaid Managed Care Organization Reimbursement Allowance Fund, exempt from section 33.080 reversion, with state treasurer recordkeeping.

headings.title: Satisfaction of section 208.431 obligation by offset or payment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an offset under section 208.435 or payment to the reimbursement allowance fund is accepted as payment of the section 208.431 obligation.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets the managed care reimbursement allowance period, delinquency enforcement, licensing consequences, tax-exempt status preservation, and the September 30, 2029 sunset for sections 208.431 to 208.437.

headings.title: Annual allowance period, balance notice, and delinquency
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a July 1 to June 30 allowance period, requires a June 30 balance notice, and makes unpaid balances delinquent after thirty days unless under appeal.

headings.title: Circuit court enforcement and Medicaid contract cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DSS to enforce unpaid allowances in circuit court and to cancel or refuse to issue, extend, or reinstate a Medicaid contract unless under appeal.

headings.title: Insurance license denial, suspension, or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Makes failure to pay a delinquent allowance grounds for the department of commerce and insurance to deny, suspend, or revoke a license unless under appeal.

headings.title: Preservation of tax-exempt and nonprofit status
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 208.431 to 208.437 do not affect or limit an organization's tax-exempt or nonprofit status.

headings.title: Expiration of sections 208.431 to 208.437
headings.reviewNote: Provides that sections 208.431 to 208.437 expire on September 30, 2029.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires MO HealthNet managed care organizations, managed care plans, and the MO HealthNet division to comply with specified prior authorization provisions of section 376.1364 by July 1, 2027, and July 1, 2028.

headings.title: July 1, 2027 compliance with section 376.1364 subsections 7 to 10
headings.reviewNote: Requires MO HealthNet managed care organizations, managed care plans, and the MO HealthNet division to comply with section 376.1364 subsections 7 to 10 by July 1, 2027.

headings.title: July 1, 2028 compliance with section 376.1364 subsections 4 to 10
headings.reviewNote: Requires MO HealthNet managed care organizations, managed care plans, and the MO HealthNet division to comply with section 376.1364 subsections 4 to 10 by July 1, 2028.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires the hospital federal reimbursement allowance formula to be set by rule under section 536.024 and designates circuit court venue for appeals. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.480).

headings.title: Hospital reimbursement allowance formula set by rule
headings.reviewNote: Requires the hospital federal reimbursement allowance formula to be established by department of social services rules promulgated under section 536.024.

headings.title: Circuit court original jurisdiction for appeals
headings.reviewNote: Designates Cole County circuit court or the circuit court where the hospital is located as the court of original jurisdiction for appeals under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs notification of hospital federal reimbursement allowance amounts, incremental payment or Medicaid offset collection, and periodic recalculation by rule. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.480).

headings.title: Director notification of reimbursement allowance amount
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department director to notify each hospital of its federal reimbursement allowance and payment or offset timing.

headings.title: Incremental payment and Medicaid offset collection
headings.reviewNote: Provides for collecting the allowance in increments over the assessment period by direct payment or offset against Medicaid payments, with offsets credited to the fund.

headings.title: Periodic recalculation of hospital reimbursement allowance
headings.reviewNote: Permits recalculating the hospital federal reimbursement allowance as prescribed by department rule.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides for protest, administrative hearing, and chapter 536 judicial review of hospital federal reimbursement allowance determinations. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.480).

headings.title: Thirty-day protest right for hospitals
headings.reviewNote: Permits a hospital to file a written protest within thirty days of notice of its federal reimbursement allowance, setting out grounds for objection.

headings.title: Administrative hearing and chapter 536 judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Requires a departmental hearing and written decision upon timely protest, subject to judicial review under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Federal Reimbursement Allowance Fund for hospital payments, treats offsets or payments as satisfying section 208.453, requires state treasurer recordkeeping, and exempts fund balances from reversion. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.480).

headings.title: Creation of Federal Reimbursement Allowance Fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs remittance of hospital allowances to DSS payable to DOR for deposit into the Federal Reimbursement Allowance Fund exclusively for hospital payments, with investment earnings credited.

headings.title: Satisfaction of section 208.453 obligation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an offset under section 208.459 or payment to the fund is accepted as payment of the hospital's section 208.453 obligation.

headings.title: State treasurer fund recordkeeping and disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state treasurer to maintain fund balance and earnings records and make them available to DSS upon written request.

headings.title: Exemption from general revenue reversion
headings.reviewNote: Exempts unexpended balances in the Federal Reimbursement Allowance Fund from biennial transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets the hospital federal reimbursement allowance period, delinquency timing, state lien enforcement, Medicaid provider agreement cancellation, and hospital licensing sanctions. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.480).

headings.title: Annual allowance period, balance notice, and delinquency
headings.reviewNote: Sets an October 1 to September 30 allowance period, requires a September 30 balance notice, and makes unpaid balances delinquent after thirty days.

headings.title: Lien enforcement and Medicaid provider agreement cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DSS to enforce a state lien against hospital property in circuit court and to cancel or refuse to issue, extend, or reinstate a Medicaid provider agreement.

headings.title: Hospital license denial, suspension, or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Makes failure to pay allowances under sections 208.450 to 208.480 (note: section 208.450 was repealed in 1994) grounds for DHSS to deny, suspend, or revoke a chapter 197 hospital license.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires Medicaid payments to participating hospitals, caps annual hospital federal reimbursement allowance levies at forty-five percent of total hospital FRA and match payments, and mandates annual legislative reports and confidential hospital disclosures. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.480).

headings.title: Medicaid payments to participating hospitals
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to make Medicaid payments to hospitals holding a Medicaid provider agreement with the department.

headings.title: Forty-five percent levy cap, legislative reporting, and hospital disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Caps annual hospital FRA levies at forty-five percent of total FRA and federal match hospital payments (note: section 208.450 was repealed in 1994), requires October 1 legislative reports, and mandates separate confidential hospital payment disclosures.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes a fiscal year 2002 funding floor for Medicaid graduate medical education appropriations starting in fiscal year 2004 and provides a contingent 180-day expiration of sections 208.453 to 208.480 if unmet. Expires September 30, 2029 (see section 208.480).

headings.title: Fiscal year 2002 funding floor for Medicaid GME payments
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual appropriations starting in fiscal year 2004 for Medicaid graduate medical education and enhanced GME payments under 13 CSR 70-15.010 to be at least fiscal year 2002 levels.

headings.title: Contingent expiration upon funding shortfall
headings.reviewNote: Expires sections 208.453 to 208.480 180 days after a fiscal year failing subsection 1 unless the department director prospectively adjusts payments to restore the prior level.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits MO HealthNet from recovering disproportionate share hospital audit recoupments from tier 1 safety net hospitals using intergovernmental transfers or paying them from general revenue; expired September 30, 2022.

headings.title: Prohibition on DSH audit recoupment from tier 1 safety net hospitals
headings.reviewNote: Bars MO HealthNet from recovering disproportionate share hospital audit recoupments from tier 1 safety net hospitals (excluding DMH psychiatric hospitals) funded via intergovernmental transfers and bars using general revenue for such federal recoupments.

headings.title: Expiration date of section
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section expires on September 30, 2022.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the short title for the Elderly Health and Nutrition Act of 1994 and defines elderly hunger, elderly person, food bank, and gatekeeper programs.

headings.title: Short title of Elderly Health and Nutrition Act of 1994
headings.reviewNote: Cites sections 208.600 to 208.630 (note: section 208.630 was repealed in 2018) as the Elderly Health and Nutrition Act of 1994.

headings.title: Definitions for elderly health and nutrition programs
headings.reviewNote: Defines elderly hunger, elderly person (age sixty or older), food bank, and gatekeeper programs for sections 208.600 to 208.630.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires the department of health and senior services to operate an ongoing public education program for at-risk elderly persons with preference for personal contacts over mass media.

headings.title: Public education program for at-risk elderly
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS in collaboration with other state agencies to implement an ongoing public education program informing at-risk elderly persons of federal and state service programs.

headings.title: Action steps favoring personal contacts
headings.reviewNote: Requires devising action steps preferring personal over mass media contacts and lists permissible methods including local grants, large-print brochures, info sessions, gatekeeper programs, and VISTA.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates an interagency task force to coordinate existing transportation resources for the elderly, directs DHSS to apply for a VISTA volunteer transportation program, and requires emergency food service models for senior housing.

headings.title: Interagency transportation coordination task force
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS, DESE, MoDOT, DMH, and DHSS to form a task force planning integration of existing transportation services for elderly and needy populations.

headings.title: VISTA application for volunteer transportation systems
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS to apply for a statewide VISTA program to organize volunteer transportation systems in communities with many at-risk elderly persons.

headings.title: Emergency food service models for senior housing
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS to devise models and provide training for senior housing facilities seeking to offer emergency food services to residents and neighbors.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires the department of elementary and secondary education to devise the Invest in Caring student volunteer program and the Intergenerational Care and Training apprenticeship program.

headings.title: Invest in Caring student volunteer model program
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE to devise the Invest in Caring model program connecting student volunteers with senior service programs for graduation or college credit.

headings.title: Intergenerational Care and Training apprenticeship program
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE to devise and implement a model apprenticeship program enabling high school senior-care volunteers to earn CNA, day care, or other job certifications or credits.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires the department of social services, with input from DMH and community agencies, to develop and deliver a report by January 1, 1995, on collaborative case management for at-risk elderly persons.

headings.title: Development of elderly case management collaboration report
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS with input from DMH and community agencies to develop a report on delivering elderly case management collaboratively across identification, transportation, nutrition, health, and socialization services.

headings.title: January 1, 1995 report delivery to governor and legislative leaders
headings.reviewNote: Requires delivering the report identifying effective methods for serving at-risk elderly to the governor, senate president pro tem, and house speaker by January 1, 1995.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the MO HealthNet uninsured children's health care program conditioned on federal SCHIP appropriations, sets income eligibility baselines, and defines children and uninsured children.

headings.title: Establishment, federal funding contingency, and eligibility baselines
headings.reviewNote: Directs MO HealthNet to establish an uninsured children's health program subject to appropriations, voids sections 208.631 to 208.658 without federal funds, and sets Title XIX and June 30, 2007 eligibility baselines.

headings.title: Definitions of children and uninsured children
headings.reviewNote: Defines children and uninsured children up to age nineteen lacking access to affordable employer-subsidized or other health coverage and excludes children eligible under section 208.151.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines affordable health coverage thresholds and cost-sharing limits for uninsured children between 150 and 300 percent of federal poverty level and directs a presumptive eligibility expansion study.

headings.title: Affordable coverage thresholds, monthly premiums, and cost-sharing limits
headings.reviewNote: Defines affordable coverage by income bracket, sets monthly premiums capped at five percent of family income and federal limits, bars cost sharing for well-baby and well-child care, and treats coverage-exhausted children as uninsured.

headings.title: Study on expanding presumptive eligibility for children
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to study expanding presumptive eligibility for children for medical assistance benefits.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires chapter 536 rulemaking for the uninsured children's health care program and federal compliance for household income determination rules.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and optional services package
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to implement the uninsured children's health program by chapter 536 rules subject to federal approval and appropriations, and permits covering section 208.152 services except nonemergency transportation.

headings.title: Determination of available income by federally compliant rule
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to determine available income by rule complying with federal laws and regulations for receiving federal program funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires DSS studies and annual reports on wraparound services, program outcomes, outreach to identify eligible uninsured children, and private insurance crowd-out above 185 percent of federal poverty level.

headings.title: Study and annual report on community wraparound services
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to commission a study and submit annual reports on community-based wraparound services for seriously emotionally disturbed and substance-abuse-affected children.

headings.title: Annual report on program enrollment, costs, and health effects
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual DSS report to the governor and general assembly detailing enrollment by income, private insurance impact, emergency room effects, resident health, state cost, and enrollment methodology.

headings.title: Outreach program to identify eligible uninsured children
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to establish an identification program for eligible nonparticipating children, including hospital coordination and a statewide education and information program.

headings.title: Private insurance crowd-out study and corrective measures
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual study on negative private-insurance impacts above 185 percent of federal poverty level and mandates corrective measures such as cost sharing, insurability tests, or open enrollment limits if measurable impact occurs.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires distributing SCHIP enrollment information through licensed child-care providers and public school districts, adds an insurance check-box to school lunch applications, bars parent penalties, authorizes rulemaking, and mandates annual reporting.

headings.title: Distribution of SCHIP information by child-care providers and schools
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS starting July 1, 2010, to supply SCHIP eligibility and application materials to funded licensed child-care providers and public school districts for distribution at enrollment.

headings.title: Free and reduced lunch application insurance inquiry and notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE to add a health-insurance check-box to free and reduced lunch applications and requires districts to send SCHIP notices to income-eligible uninsured families.

headings.title: Exclusive use of department-developed SCHIP notices
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to develop the subsection 2 notice with enrollment information and prohibits distributing any other SCHIP notice under this section.

headings.title: Prohibition on penalties against parents or guardians
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits assessing any penalty on parents or guardians who fail to provide or provide inaccurate information under this section.

headings.title: Permissive rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Permits DESE and DSS to adopt implementing rules subject to chapter 536 and makes the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers after August 28, 2010.

headings.title: Annual DESE and DSS report on lunch applications and SCHIP outreach
headings.reviewNote: Requires DESE and DSS to report annually to the governor and legislative budget chairs on free/reduced lunch families, uninsured indicators, notices sent, and resulting SCHIP applications.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Show-Me Healthy Babies Program as a separate CHIP program for low-income unborn children, governs eligibility, prenatal and postpartum coverage, outreach, federal waivers, annual cost-savings reports, and nonentitlement status.

headings.title: Establishment of Show-Me Healthy Babies Program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Show-Me Healthy Babies Program within DSS as a separate Title XXI CHIP program for low-income unborn children.

headings.title: Eligibility criteria and family size calculation
headings.reviewNote: Sets income eligibility up to 300 percent of federal poverty level for unborn children whose mothers are ineligible for Medicaid and lack affordable coverage, counting all unborn children in family size.

headings.title: Scope of prenatal and pregnancy-related coverage
headings.reviewNote: Covers prenatal care, pregnancy-related services benefiting the unborn child, and childbirth education classes, excluding services solely for the mother while permitting 42 U.S.C. 1397ll assistance.

headings.title: No waiting period, presumptive eligibility, and pregnancy verification
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits waiting periods, covers conception to birth, requires a presumptive eligibility procedure, and mandates pregnancy verification.

headings.title: Postnatal child coverage for up to one year
headings.reviewNote: Continues coverage for the child for up to one year after birth unless otherwise prohibited by law or limited by appropriations.

headings.title: Maternal postpartum coverage and twelve-month extension
headings.reviewNote: Provides sixty-day postpartum coverage and, subject to federal approval and section 208.239 redetermination triggers beginning July 6, 2023, twelve-month postpartum coverage while federal authority remains in effect.

headings.title: Delivery of coverage in same manner as county CHIP
headings.reviewNote: Requires providing coverage for enrolled unborn children in the same manner as CHIP coverage in the mother's county of primary residence.

headings.title: Information sharing with maternity homes and pregnancy resource centers
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to provide program information to maternity homes, pregnancy resource centers, and similar agencies and consider allowing them to assist with enrollment, presumptive eligibility, and pregnancy verification.

headings.title: Federal state plan amendment or waiver submission
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS within sixty days after August 28, 2014, to submit a state plan amendment or waiver request to federal HHS for program approval.

headings.title: Annual cost-savings and benefits report
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual DSS report to the governor and legislative leaders analyzing and projecting public and private cost savings and health benefits from enrolling unborn children.

headings.title: Nonentitlement status and appropriation contingency
headings.reviewNote: Declares the program not an entitlement and subjects it to federal allotments or appropriations and matching state appropriations.

headings.title: No state obligation if federal or state funding ends
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not obligate the state to continue the program if federal allotments end or are insufficient or if the general assembly does not appropriate funds.

headings.title: Construction against MO HealthNet expansion or federal mandate
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not expand MO HealthNet or fulfill a federal mandate imposed on the state.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines telehealth terms for MO HealthNet and mandates provider reimbursement parity with in-person care without originating-site or distance restrictions.

headings.title: Definitions for MO HealthNet telehealth
headings.reviewNote: Defines consultation, distant site, originating site, provider, and telehealth by reference to CPT and section 191.1145.

headings.title: Telehealth reimbursement parity and store-and-forward cap
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to reimburse telehealth meeting in-person standards of care without originating-site or distance restrictions, considers originating-site reimbursement, and permits capping asynchronous store-and-forward at in-person rates.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes a MO HealthNet home telemonitoring reimbursement program subject to appropriations, sets clinical eligibility criteria, permits discontinuance if not cost effective, and requires Medicare savings review, federal waivers, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Establishment and definition of home telemonitoring program
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS, subject to appropriations, to establish a statewide MO HealthNet home telemonitoring reimbursement program transmitting scheduled data to a URAC-accredited health call center.

headings.title: Eligible conditions, risk factors, physician sharing, and nonduplication
headings.reviewNote: Limits eligibility to specified diagnoses combined with two or more risk factors, requires sharing clinical data with the participant's physician, and bars duplicating MO HealthNet disease management.

headings.title: Permissive discontinuance if not cost effective
headings.reviewNote: Permits DSS to discontinue the home telemonitoring program and reimbursement if it determines after implementation that the program is not cost effective.

headings.title: Evaluation of Medicare cost savings for dual eligibles
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to determine whether home telemonitoring for dually eligible MO HealthNet and Medicare beneficiaries achieves Medicare cost savings.

headings.title: Federal waiver request and implementation delay
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to request any necessary federal waiver or authorization before implementing a provision and permits delaying implementation until granted.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 and makes the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers after August 28, 2016.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the short title for the Missouri Long-term Care Partnership Program Act and defines asset disregard, qualified partnership policies, MO HealthNet, and state plan amendment.

headings.title: Short title of Missouri Long-term Care Partnership Program Act
headings.reviewNote: Cites sections 208.690 to 208.698 as the Missouri Long-term Care Partnership Program Act.

headings.title: Definitions for long-term care partnership program
headings.reviewNote: Defines asset disregard, Missouri qualified long-term care partnership approved policy, MO HealthNet, and state plan amendment.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Long-Term Care Partnership Program, mandates asset disregard in MO HealthNet eligibility and estate recovery, sets DSS state plan and training duties, and requires rulemaking.

headings.title: Establishment and purposes of long-term care partnership program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri Long-Term Care Partnership Program administered by DSS with DCI to encourage private long-term care insurance and reduce MO HealthNet financial burden.

headings.title: Asset disregard for MO HealthNet eligibility, payment, and recovery
headings.reviewNote: Requires disregarding qualifying partnership policy benefit amounts when determining MO HealthNet eligibility, payment amounts, and subsequent state recovery.

headings.title: State plan amendment application and DCI training assistance
