headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS within 180 days of August 28, 2007, to apply for a federal state plan amendment and provide technical assistance to DCI for producer training.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 and makes the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers after August 28, 2007.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants MO HealthNet asset disregard eligibility to qualified partnership policy beneficiaries, preserves disregard if the program is discontinued, and authorizes interstate reciprocity agreements.

headings.title: Eligibility for MO HealthNet asset disregard
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that a beneficiary of a Missouri qualified long-term care partnership-approved policy is eligible for MO HealthNet using asset disregard.

headings.title: Preservation of asset disregard upon program discontinuance
headings.reviewNote: Preserves asset disregard eligibility under federal law for individuals who purchased a qualified partnership policy before any discontinuance of the Missouri program.

headings.title: Interstate reciprocal asset disregard agreements
headings.reviewNote: Permits DSS to enter reciprocal agreements with other Deficit Reduction Act partnership states to extend asset disregard to Missouri residents purchasing out-of-state policies.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs the department of commerce and insurance director on partnership policy producer training, uniform policy standards and inflation protection, consumer notices, policy exchanges, and certification rulemaking.

headings.title: Insurance director duties for partnership policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the DCI director to establish producer training, avoid partnership-only policy mandates except federal inflation protection, develop consumer summary notices, and ensure equitable policy exchanges.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking for certification and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires the DCI director to promulgate implementing and policy-certification rules under chapter 536 and makes the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers after August 28, 2007.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the short title for the Family Development Account Program and defines statutory terms including account holder, community-based organization, reserve fund, financial institution, and program contributor.

headings.title: Short title of Family Development Account Program
headings.reviewNote: Cites sections 208.750 to 208.775 as the Family Development Account Program.

headings.title: Definitions for Family Development Account Program
headings.reviewNote: Defines ten terms including account holder, community-based organization, department, director, family development account, reserve fund, federal poverty level, financial institution, program, and program contributor.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Family Development Account Program within the department of economic development, governs community-based organization proposals and review factors, caps reserve fund administrative costs, and mandates rulemaking.

headings.title: Establishment of Family Development Account Program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Family Development Account Program in the department of economic development for savings dedicated to education, home ownership, or small business capitalization.

headings.title: Solicitation and required contents of community-based organization proposals
headings.reviewNote: Requires soliciting nonprofit CBO proposals specifying cash match rules, investment input, priority populations, economic literacy seminars, and compliance evaluation.

headings.title: Department review criteria for organization proposals
headings.reviewNote: Lists five factors DED must consider when reviewing CBO proposals, including nonprofit status, fiscal accountability, fundraising, reserve fund administration, and auxiliary services.

headings.title: Caps on reserve fund administrative expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Caps reserve fund administrative costs at twenty percent in the first two years and fifteen percent thereafter, and bars using account-holder deposits for administrative costs.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Requires DED to promulgate rules implementing sections 208.750 to 208.775 pursuant to chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets income eligibility and penalty-free withdrawal purposes for family development accounts, governs approved financial institution certification and account duties including up to three-to-one matching, and caps annual deposits and total balances.

headings.title: Income eligibility and approved penalty-free withdrawals
headings.reviewNote: Permits households at or below 200 percent of federal poverty level to open accounts and withdraw funds with CBO approval for higher education, job training, primary home purchase or repair, or small business start-up.

headings.title: Approved financial institutions and deposit certification
headings.reviewNote: Permits department-approved financial institutions to establish accounts and requires them to certify account establishment and deposits to the department.

headings.title: Financial institution account duties and matching deposits
headings.reviewNote: Requires financial institutions to hold accounts in the holder's name, accept holder and up to three-to-one CBO matching deposits, pay at least market interest, and allow approved withdrawals.

headings.title: Annual deposit limit and maximum account balance
headings.reviewNote: Caps annual account-holder deposits at $2,000 per calendar year and total account balances at $50,000.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires forfeiture of matching moneys upon unauthorized withdrawal from a family development account, returns forfeited moneys to the community-based organization reserve fund, and governs transfer upon an account holder's death.

headings.title: Forfeiture of matching moneys for unauthorized withdrawal
headings.reviewNote: Requires account holders who withdraw moneys outside section 208.760(1) purposes to forfeit all matching moneys in the account.

headings.title: Return of forfeited moneys to organization reserve fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs all moneys forfeited under subsection 1 back to the community-based organization's family development account reserve fund.

headings.title: Transfer to contingent beneficiary or reserve fund upon death
headings.reviewNote: Permits transferring an account to a named contingent beneficiary upon the account holder's death, or to the CBO reserve fund if the beneficiary is deceased or unable to accept.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts family development account deposits, approved withdrawals, and earned interest from state taxation, disregards balances for public assistance, authorizes a fifty-percent contributor tax credit verified by DED, and sets annual statewide credit caps.

headings.title: Tax exemption for deposits and approved withdrawals
headings.reviewNote: Exempts family development account deposits and approved section 208.760(1) withdrawals from chapter 143, 147, 148, and 153 taxes (excluding withholding tax), while taxing unapproved withdrawals.

headings.title: Income tax exemption for account interest
headings.reviewNote: Exempts interest earned by a family development account from chapter 143 income taxation.

headings.title: Disregard of account funds for public assistance
headings.reviewNote: Requires disregarding family development account funds and accrued interest when determining eligibility for or amounts of public assistance or benefits.

headings.title: Fifty-percent tax credit for program contributors
headings.reviewNote: Allows program contributors a tax credit of up to fifty percent on contributions up to $50,000 against chapter 143 (excluding withholding), 147, 148, and 153 taxes.

headings.title: Department verification and contributor reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires CBO administrators and participating financial institutions to report annual contributor totals to DED for tax credit verification and submission to DOR.

headings.title: Annual statewide tax credit caps
headings.reviewNote: Caps total authorized tax credits at $4 million per fiscal year through June 30, 2010, and $300,000 per fiscal year beginning July 1, 2010.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Rx Plan within DSS to coordinate prescription drug benefits with Medicare Part D, authorizes preferred plan auto-enrollment with notices, mandates rulemaking, permits delegation and contracting, and requires interagency assistance. Terminates August 28, 2029 (see section 208.798).

headings.title: Establishment and purpose of Missouri Rx Plan
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri Rx Plan within DSS as a state pharmaceutical assistance program for eligible elderly and disabled residents coordinating with Medicare Part D.

headings.title: Part D coordination, preferred plans, and preliminary enrollment notices
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes coordinating with Part D, selecting preferred PDPs, and preliminarily enrolling beneficiaries with four mandatory opt-out and nonpreferred-plan notices (original rolls include the word 'That' in subdivision (4)).

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate implementing rules including benefit limits under chapter 536 and makes the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers after August 28, 2005.

headings.title: Delegation of administration and contracting authority
headings.reviewNote: Permits DSS to delegate administrative responsibilities and contract with other states, purchasing pools, or for-profit or nonprofit entities.

headings.title: Interagency assistance and information sharing
headings.reviewNote: Requires other state agencies upon DSS request to provide assistance or information necessary to administer the Missouri Rx Plan.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes Missouri Rx Plan eligibility criteria, dual-eligible and low-income enrollment priorities with opt-out automatic enrollment, and attestation-based applications for non-dual eligibles. Terminates August 28, 2029 (see section 208.798).

headings.title: Eligibility criteria for Part D coordination
headings.reviewNote: Coordinates Part D prescription coverage for Missouri residents age sixty-five or older or disabled Medicare beneficiaries enrolled in Part D who are not in an MMA-subsidized retirement plan.

headings.title: Enrollment priorities and dual-eligible automatic enrollment
headings.reviewNote: Prioritizes Medicaid dual eligibles first and Medicare applicants at or below 150 percent of federal poverty guidelines meeting the asset test second, and permits automatic enrollment of dual eligibles with an opt-out right.

headings.title: Application and attestation for non-dual eligibles
headings.reviewNote: Permits eligible non-dual-eligible individuals or married couples to apply by submitting an application attesting to age, residence, household income, and liquid assets.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerates DSS administrative powers for the Missouri Rx Plan including manufacturer rebates and preferred plan enrollment, sets the January 1, 2006 benefit start date, and authorizes cost-sharing payments subject to appropriation. Terminates August 28, 2029 (see section 208.798).

headings.title: Department powers, manufacturer rebates, and contracting
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes DSS to adopt rules, contract with Part D plans, require Medicaid-level manufacturer rebates for enrollees at or below 200 percent FPL with non-appropriated revenue deposited in the fund, preliminarily enroll with opt-out, prescribe procedures, and procure contractors.

headings.title: January 1, 2006 benefit start date and cost-sharing payments
headings.reviewNote: Starts program benefits on January 1, 2006, and permits paying Part D deductibles, coinsurance, premiums, and copayments subject to appropriation and available funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Declares the Missouri Rx Plan a nonentitlement payer of last resort subject to annual appropriations and defines ineligibility or reduced assistance for applicants with other drug coverage. Terminates August 28, 2029 (see section 208.798).

headings.title: Nonentitlement status and annual appropriation limits
headings.reviewNote: Declares the program not an entitlement and limits benefits to appropriated funds less gubernatorial withholdings or reductions.

headings.title: Payer of last resort status
headings.reviewNote: Designates the program as payer of last resort covering only participant costs not covered by Medicare Part D.

headings.title: Ineligibility for other public assistance drug coverage
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies applicants qualified for prescription coverage under another public assistance program other than MMA benefits, except dual eligibles transitioning from Medicaid.

headings.title: Ineligibility for full third-party prescription coverage
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies applicants eligible for full prescription drug coverage under another assistance or insurance plan.

headings.title: Reduced assistance for partial third-party coverage
headings.reviewNote: Allows applicants with partial prescription drug coverage under another insurance plan to receive reduced Missouri Rx assistance.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes fixed Missouri residency requirements, household income caps at 185 percent of federal poverty level converted to MAGI equivalent, and mandatory rulemaking for residency and income documentation. Terminates August 28, 2029 (see section 208.798).

headings.title: Fixed Missouri residency requirement and applicant burden
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants, including long-term care facility residents, to have or intend a fixed permanent Missouri residence and places the burden of proof on the applicant.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking for residency documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate rules establishing residency documentation standards requiring documents with the applicant's Missouri name and address.

headings.title: Household income cap subject to appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Subjects eligibility income limits to appropriations and caps household income at 185 percent of federal poverty level converted to the MAGI equivalent net income standard.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking for income documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to promulgate rules establishing standards for documenting household income.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Missouri Rx Plan Fund in the state treasury, designates state treasurer custody and investment authority, retains program collections, and exempts fund balances from biennial reversion. Terminates August 28, 2029 (see section 208.798).

headings.title: Creation of Missouri Rx Plan Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Rx Plan Fund in the state treasury consisting of program deposits and appropriations from federal or other sources.

headings.title: State treasurer custody, investments, and dedicated use
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state treasurer as custodian, restricts appropriated disbursements to sections 208.780 to 208.798 administration, credits investment earnings to the fund, and bars general revenue reversion.

headings.title: Retention of program collections and revenues
headings.reviewNote: Directs that all funds collected by or due and payable to the Missouri Rx Plan Fund remain in and accrue to the fund.

headings.title: Exemption from biennial general revenue reversion
headings.reviewNote: Exempts fund moneys from biennial reversion to general revenue under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes one-time transition grants up to $2,400 for MO HealthNet-eligible nursing home residents moving into the community and requires DHSS and DMH to develop community-service training and rules.

headings.title: Nursing home transition grants for community re-entry
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes subject to appropriations one-time transition grants up to $2,400 administered by the division of senior and disability services with DSS, and directs seeking federal and private grants.

headings.title: Community service training, mandatory rulemaking, and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS and DMH to develop community-based service information and training, promulgate rules under chapter 536, and makes the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers after August 28, 2009.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes DHSS referral processing timelines and applicant choice disclosures for MO HealthNet home- and community-based services, permits provider assessments after missed deadlines, mandates audits, defines terms, and requires an automated care plan tool and 2014 legislative report.

headings.title: Referral processing timelines, applicant disclosures, and prioritization
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS upon receiving a completed HCBS referral or physician order to act within fifteen business days, send address and ten-day notices, disclose service and provider choices, and prioritize high-risk and hotline referrals.

headings.title: Provider assessment option and five-day automatic approval
headings.reviewNote: Permits a provider to complete an assessment and care plan recommendation if DHSS misses the fifteen-day deadline, with automatic approval and payment if DHSS does not act within five business days.

headings.title: Effective care plan and nonliability for ineligible level of care
headings.reviewNote: Makes the latest DHSS-approved or modified care plan effective and relieves the state of liability for services claimed before written denial if the client fails to meet the level of care.

headings.title: Implementation subject to federal CMS approval
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS to implement subsections 2 and 3 unless CMS disapproves necessary state plan amendments or waivers allowing provider assessments.

headings.title: Statistically valid provider audits and public process review
headings.reviewNote: Requires statistically valid DHSS auditing of provider care plans, assessments, and choice disclosures and public availability of its participant-information process review.

headings.title: Definitions of assessment and properly completed referral
headings.reviewNote: Defines face-to-face assessment requirements and minimum information required for a properly completed HCBS referral.

headings.title: Automated electronic assessment care plan tool and recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS to develop an automated electronic assessment care plan tool for providers and submit implementation recommendations to the general assembly by January 1, 2014.

headings.title: December 31, 2014 report to the general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS by December 31, 2014, to report to the general assembly on fifteen-day compliance, assessor approval, program costs, outside assessment audits, and staffing policies.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs DSS to apply for a federal Section 1915(c) structured family caregiver waiver for MO HealthNet participants with Alzheimer's or related disorders, specifies nine waiver requirements, and requires DHSS implementing rules upon waiver approval.

headings.title: Federal waiver application for structured family caregiving
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to apply to federal HHS for a Section 1915(c) structured family caregiver waiver as an agency-directed model for participants with Alzheimer's or related disorders, subject to federal approval.

headings.title: Mandatory waiver terms, 300-participant cap, and rate limits
headings.reviewNote: Specifies nine required waiver elements including full-time co-residing caregivers, family care safety registry, liability insurance, 300-participant cap, agency duties, personal care tasks, a 35-percent agency cap, and a 60-percent nursing home cost cap.

headings.title: Ninety-day waiver filing deadline and mandatory DHSS rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to apply within ninety days of August 28, 2019, seeking an effective date before July 2, 2020, and requires DHSS upon waiver approval to promulgate rules subject to chapter 536 nonseverability.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets eligibility criteria for consumer-directed personal care assistance financial assistance and defines vendor payroll, Medicaid claiming, statewide rate setting, and consumer-employer status.

headings.title: Eligibility requirements for consumer-directed personal care assistance
headings.reviewNote: Requires providing financial assistance subject to appropriations through eligible vendors to physically disabled Medicaid-eligible adults capable of independent living and self-direction needing nursing-home-level care within average nursing facility costs.

headings.title: Vendor payroll and claiming duties and employer status
headings.reviewNote: Assigns vendors payroll, fringe benefit accounting, and Medicaid claiming, directs the department to set the statewide rate, and clarifies the attendant is the consumer's employee only during subsidized hours and not an employee of the vendor, department, or state.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes eligibility determination and annual reverification timelines using a common assessment tool, ten-day eligibility notices, personal care service plan contents, vendor selection, and annual needs reevaluation.

headings.title: Eligibility determination and reverification timelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires reverifying pre-August 28, 2005 consumers within one year, initiating new applicant determinations within thirty days, reverifying every twelve months using the common assessment tool, and complying with section 208.909(3) (original rolls reference 'subsection 2').

headings.title: Ten-day notice of initial eligibility determination
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the applicant of the department's initial eligibility determination within ten days.

headings.title: Contents of personal care assistance services plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires developing a personal care assistance services plan stating maximum fifteen-minute service units and initiation and reverification dates.

headings.title: Consumer vendor selection and signed plan distribution
headings.reviewNote: Requires eligible consumers to select an eligible vendor maintaining an eligible attendant list, with the signed plan distributed to the consumer, vendor, and department.

headings.title: Annual reevaluation of consumer needs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to reevaluate consumer needs annually and maintain, adjust, or eliminate authorized assistance accordingly.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines consumer and vendor responsibilities for personal care assistance, bars funding routine household tasks and unscreened attendants, mandates vendor telephone tracking systems with rulemaking, and imposes vendor tax-garnishment liability and penalties.

headings.title: Consumer responsibilities in personal care assistance
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates eight consumer duties including supervising attendants, verifying wages, submitting biweekly signed timesheets, ten-day change notice, reporting quality problems, EIN paperwork, allowing monitoring visits, and reporting health changes.

headings.title: Vendor responsibilities in personal care assistance
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates six vendor duties including certifying timesheets, Medicaid claiming, direct attendant payment, timely payroll tax payment, annual face-to-face plan monitoring, and reporting health or self-direction changes.

headings.title: Prohibition on funding routine shared household tasks
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits state or federal payment for services primarily benefiting the household unit or typical shared household tasks unless above and beyond activities for a household member without a disability.

headings.title: Background screening requirement for personal care attendants
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits paying state or federal funds for attendants without section 192.2495 background screening or with a disqualifying finding absent a good-cause waiver.

headings.title: Mandatory vendor telephone tracking system and DHSS rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Requires vendors by July 1, 2015, to use a telephone tracking system meeting seven criteria, permits advanced replacements, and mandates DHSS rulemaking subject to chapter 536 nonseverability after August 28, 2010.

headings.title: Vendor tax-garnishment liability, notice duty, and penalty
headings.reviewNote: Makes vendors liable to consumers for garnishments from unpaid payroll taxes, requires forwarding tax delinquency notices, and permits a $1,000 penalty per occurrence.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates abuse and neglect reporting for personal care assistance consumers with criminal penalties for nonreporting, governs investigations, temporary protection orders, confidentiality, immunity, anti-retaliation, and employee disqualification list placement and distribution.

headings.title: Mandatory abuse and neglect reporting by enumerated persons
headings.reviewNote: Requires listed health professionals, vendors, attendants, and agency employees to immediately report suspected consumer abuse or neglect and requires maintaining contact with reporting physicians.

headings.title: Investigation of deteriorating physical condition reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the department case manager and nurse upon reports of deteriorating physical condition and immediate investigation and reporting to the nurse.

headings.title: Volunteer abuse-detection training by area agencies on aging
headings.reviewNote: Requires local area agencies on aging, if requested, to provide volunteer training to mandatory reporters on detecting and reporting abuse and neglect.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for failure to report
headings.reviewNote: Makes a mandatory reporter's failure to report suspected abuse or neglect within a reasonable time a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Required contents of abuse and neglect reports
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required report details including names and addresses of the vendor, attendant, and consumer, nature of abuse or neglect, and complainant name.

headings.title: Permissive reporting by other persons
headings.reviewNote: Permits any other person with reasonable cause to believe a consumer was abused or neglected by an attendant to report to the department.

headings.title: Director referral and temporary care protection petitions
headings.reviewNote: Requires referring substantiated complaints to the director or designee and authorizes circuit court petitions (mandatory for the attorney general upon request) for ex parte thirty-day temporary protection orders.

headings.title: Confidentiality of abuse and neglect reports
headings.reviewNote: Makes abuse and neglect reports confidential as provided under section 192.2500.

headings.title: Civil and criminal immunity for reporters and witnesses
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and criminal immunity to reporters and witnesses (excluding abusers, perjury, negligence, recklessness, bad faith, or malice).

headings.title: Five-working-day notice of report receipt and investigation
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the reporter within five working days of receiving a mandatory report and initiating the investigation.

headings.title: Prohibition on vendor or attendant retaliation against consumers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits vendors and personal care attendants from harassing, dismissing, or retaliating against a consumer for reporting suspected legal or regulatory violations.

headings.title: Placement on employee disqualification list for abuse or neglect
headings.reviewNote: Requires placing persons finally determined to have recklessly, knowingly, or purposely abused or neglected a consumer on the section 192.2490 employee disqualification list.

headings.title: Distribution of employee disqualification list to vendors
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to provide the section 192.2490 employee disqualification list to vendors defined in section 208.900.

headings.title: Immunity for declining to employ or terminating listed persons
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from suit to list recipients and health care providers who decline to employ or terminate a person listed on the employee disqualification list.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes reporting misappropriation of consumer property or falsification of personal care delivery records, establishes a class A misdemeanor, mandates investigation and law enforcement reporting, and governs confidentiality, immunity, anti-retaliation, and employee disqualification listing.

headings.title: Permissive reporting of misappropriation or document falsification
headings.reviewNote: Permits any person with reasonable cause to believe consumer property or funds were misappropriated or service delivery documents falsified to report to the department.

headings.title: Information obtained by department for reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to attempt to obtain vendor, attendant, and consumer names and addresses, nature of misappropriation or falsification, and complainant details.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for misappropriation or falsification
headings.reviewNote: Makes a vendor's or attendant's conversion of consumer property or funds or falsification of service delivery documents a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Immediate investigation and law enforcement reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department upon receiving a report to immediately initiate an investigation and report gained information to appropriate law enforcement authorities.

headings.title: Referral of probable findings to department director
headings.reviewNote: Requires investigators to refer complaints and reports indicating probable misappropriation or document falsification to the department director or designee.

headings.title: Confidentiality of misappropriation reports
headings.reviewNote: Makes reports under this section confidential as provided under section 192.2500.

headings.title: Civil and criminal immunity for reporters and witnesses
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and criminal immunity to reporters and witnesses (excluding participants or beneficiaries, perjury, negligence, recklessness, bad faith, or malice).

headings.title: Five-working-day written notice to reporter
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the reporter in writing within five working days of receiving a required report and initiating the investigation.

headings.title: Prohibition on vendor retaliation against consumers or attendants
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits vendor agency authorities from harassing, dismissing, or retaliating against a consumer or attendant for reporting suspected legal or regulatory violations.

headings.title: Placement on employee disqualification list for misappropriation or falsification
headings.reviewNote: Requires placing attendants and vendor employees finally determined under section 192.2490 to have misappropriated consumer property or funds or falsified service documents on the employee disqualification list.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets independent-living philosophy and six service requirements for personal care assistance vendors, ongoing financial audit, outcome reporting, quality assurance, and business-location duties, and restricts vendor employees from conducting home visits for their own attendant clients.

headings.title: Vendor independent-living philosophy and six qualifying services
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualifying vendors to promote independent living and provide consumer orientation with fraud notice, recruitment training, an eligible attendant list, inquiry processing, family care safety registry enrollment, and telephone tracking.

headings.title: Ongoing vendor financial, reporting, quality assurance, and location duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires maintaining vendor agreements via quarterly financial reports and CPA audits or reviews, service outcome reports, quality assurance with DHSS manager-course rulemaking and annual home visits, statutory compliance, and a compliant business location starting July 1, 2022.

headings.title: Restriction on vendor employees visiting their own attendant clients
headings.reviewNote: Bars state or federal payment if a direct vendor employee conducts the face-to-face home visit for a consumer for whom the employee also serves as attendant beyond three temporary days in a thirty-day period.

entries.reviewSummary: Entitles personal care assistance applicants and consumers to a department of social services hearing on denials, service reductions, plan disputes, or discontinuations, and sets a ninety-day written request procedure.

headings.title: Entitlement to department of social services hearing
headings.reviewNote: Grants personal care assistance applicants and consumers a right to a DSS hearing upon denial of eligibility, insufficient service level, plan disputes, or discontinuation under section 208.924.

headings.title: Ninety-day written request and section 208.080 procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires requesting a hearing in writing to DSS within ninety days after mailing or delivery of DHSS's written decision under section 208.080 procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Lists six grounds for discontinuing a consumer's personal care assistance services and requires attendants to report significant consumer health deterioration or inability to self-direct care.

headings.title: Grounds for discontinuing personal care assistance services
headings.reviewNote: Permits discontinuing services for case-closure events, falsification or fraud, persistent plan noncompliance, threats or abuse endangering welfare, plan hours exceeding availability, or unresolved attendant nonperformance.

headings.title: Attendant duty to report health deterioration or lost self-direction
headings.reviewNote: Requires personal care attendants to report to the department if they witness significant consumer health deterioration or believe the consumer can no longer self-direct care.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes non-MO HealthNet consumer-directed personal care financial assistance for pre-July 2005 participants, governs income and asset limits, documentation, plans, premiums, nonpayment termination, annual reevaluation, hearings, rulemaking, and the June 30, 2025 expiration date.

headings.title: Definition of department
headings.reviewNote: Defines department as the department of health and senior services for purposes of this section.

headings.title: Non-MO HealthNet financial assistance eligibility and payer of last resort
headings.reviewNote: Permits DHSS subject to appropriations to provide personal care assistance to June 30, 2005 non-MO HealthNet participants (note: referenced sections 178.661 to 178.673 were repealed in 2005) lacking affordable coverage, as payer of last resort.

headings.title: Financial need, 300-percent income cap, and $250,000 asset limit
headings.reviewNote: Requires demonstrating financial need based on consumer and spouse AGI less disability-related medical expenses at or below 300 percent of federal poverty level and assets not exceeding $250,000.

headings.title: Required documentation of income, assets, and medical expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants, consumers, and spouses to provide tax returns and specified income, wage, bank, and disability-related medical expense documentation.

headings.title: Development of personal care assistance services plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires DHSS to develop a section 208.906 personal care assistance services plan stating the maximum financial assistance allowed subject to appropriation.

headings.title: Monthly participant premium and five-percent income cap
headings.reviewNote: Requires each participating consumer to pay a monthly premium equal to the MCHCP average premium, capped at five percent of consumer and spouse AGI.

headings.title: Denial, sixty-day termination, and reenrollment for premium nonpayment
headings.reviewNote: Denies or terminates assistance for premium nonpayment absent good cause, terminates enrollment after sixty consecutive days of nonpayment, and requires paying past-due and current premiums to reenroll.

headings.title: Annual financial reevaluation and ten-day verification notices
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reevaluation of eligibility and financial need with ten-day response and ten-day appeal-or-closure letters and spouse/consumer documentation.

headings.title: Ninety-day DSS hearing right and continuation during appeal
headings.reviewNote: Grants applicants and consumers a DSS hearing right within ninety days under section 208.080 with services continuing during the appeal process.

headings.title: Applicability of sections 208.900 to 208.927
headings.reviewNote: Applies all other provisions of sections 208.900 to 208.927 unless otherwise provided in this section.

headings.title: Permissive rulemaking and voiding of inconsistent DESE rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits DHSS to promulgate rules and emergency rules under chapter 536 and voids inconsistent DESE 5 CSR 90-7 rules (source note: rules moved to 19 CSR 15-8 effective August 29, 2005).

headings.title: June 30, 2025 expiration date
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the provisions of this section expire on June 30, 2025.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires DSS to create MO HealthNet health improvement plans with quality penalties, universal enrollment and health care homes, guiding principles, exemptions for aged/blind/disabled from mandatory risk-bearing plans, an independent outcomes survey, public input, health risk assessments, and competitive procurement.

headings.title: Creation of MO HealthNet health improvement plans and quality penalties
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS with MO HealthNet Oversight Committee advice and approval to create health improvement plans between July 1, 2008, and July 1, 2011, with contract penalties for unmet quality targets including nonemergency emergency-room use.

headings.title: Universal enrollment, health care homes, and plan evaluations
headings.reviewNote: Requires enrolling every participant in a health improvement plan with a health care home, domestic call centers, annual satisfaction reports, evidence-based practices, and DSS comparative evaluations reported to the oversight committee.

headings.title: Guiding principles for health improvement plan rules and policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires plan rules and policies to align with transparency, personal responsibility, prevention, performance-based assessments, improved outcomes, access, and cost-effective technology and care coordination.

headings.title: Exemption of aged, blind, or disabled from mandatory risk-bearing plans
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that no state law requires any aged, blind, or disabled person to enroll in a risk-bearing coordination plan.

headings.title: Independent survey of health outcomes and provider availability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS by July 1, 2008, to commission an independent six-month survey of health outcomes, specialty provider demographics, and satisfaction, giving preference to Missouri-based organizations.

headings.title: Public stakeholder process for plan design and implementation
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to engage consumers, health and disability advocates, providers, and other stakeholders in a public design and implementation process.

headings.title: Mandatory health risk assessments and individualized care plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires all health improvement plans by July 1, 2008, to conduct health risk assessments and develop individualized care plans with achievable health goals.

headings.title: Competitive requests for proposals for MO HealthNet contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires competitive requests for proposals consistent with chapter 34 or chapter 630 state procurement processes for MO HealthNet administrative contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the permanent ten-member Joint Committee on Public Assistance, requires annual agency caseload reports, governs meetings, public testimony, staffing, and an annual rolling five-year forecast report. Source note: effective August 28, 2016 (S.B. 607) and October 14, 2016 (S.B. 608, veto overridden September 14, 2016).

headings.title: Establishment, purposes, and agency data access of Joint Committee on Public Assistance
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the permanent Joint Committee on Public Assistance to monitor program efficacy, resource adequacy, and legislative recommendations and to obtain MO HealthNet, SNAP, and TANF data from state departments.

headings.title: Annual agency caseload reports to committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires the directors of DSS, DMH, and DHSS to submit annual written reports providing employee caseload data for public assistance programs.

headings.title: Ten-member legislative composition and party balance
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a ten-member legislative committee from budget, appropriations, and public assistance committees plus leadership appointees, with no more than four members per chamber from one party.

headings.title: Selection of committee chair
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the members of the committee shall select a chair.

headings.title: Semiannual meetings, public testimony, and expert input
headings.reviewNote: Requires meeting at least twice a year with time for public testimony and seeking recommendations from social, economic, and public assistance experts.

headings.title: Staff hiring authority and contingent-fund expenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes hiring staff including an executive director with house speaker and senate president pro tem approval, funded from legislative contingent funds until appropriated.

headings.title: Annual rolling five-year forecast and January 1 legislative report
headings.reviewNote: Requires conducting a rolling five-year public assistance forecast and submitting an annual report to the general assembly by January 1 starting in 2018.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the nineteen-member MO HealthNet Oversight Committee in DSS, governs member appointments, terms, support, and twelve oversight and reporting duties, and exempts sections 208.950 to 208.955 from the Missouri Sunset Act.

headings.title: Establishment and nineteen-member composition of MO HealthNet Oversight Committee
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the nineteen-member MO HealthNet Oversight Committee within DSS by January 1, 2008, specifying legislative, provider, consumer, advocate, public, and ex officio agency director seats.

headings.title: Appointments, terms, support, and twelve enumerated committee duties
headings.reviewNote: Governs gubernatorial appointments, staggered terms, expense reimbursement, DSS support, and twelve duties including quarterly meetings, section 208.950 reviews, annual reports starting January 1, 2009, federal drawdown and demographic review, an inspector general study, and rulemaking recommendations.

headings.title: Exemption from Missouri Sunset Act
headings.reviewNote: Exempts sections 208.950 to 208.955 from the Missouri Sunset Act under section 23.253.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets federal 42 CFR 435 eligibility requirements for MO HealthNet, mandates annual redeterminations and electronic data searches, governs application documentation, and specifies MAGI eligibility rules for section 208.991 coverage.

headings.title: Federal 42 CFR 435 eligibility criteria for MO HealthNet
headings.reviewNote: Requires MO HealthNet applicants to meet 42 CFR 435 criteria including Missouri residency, valid Social Security number, citizenship or verified qualified alien status, and pregnancy verification.

headings.title: Annual eligibility redeterminations and administrative contracting
headings.reviewNote: Requires the family support division effective January 1, 2014, to conduct annual redeterminations under 42 CFR 435.916 and permits contracting with an administrative service organization if cost effective.

headings.title: Electronic data searches for redetermination and final authority
headings.reviewNote: Requires conducting electronic data searches on income, residency, citizenship, and identity, permits vendor contracting, and retains final eligibility authority with DSS.

headings.title: Application compliance with 42 CFR 435.907 and documentation duty
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting MO HealthNet applications under 42 CFR 435.907 and providing required documentation to determine eligibility or resolve redetermination discrepancies.

headings.title: Additional eligibility rules for section 208.991 MAGI coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires section 208.991 applicants to meet 42 CFR 435 and 457 rules including projected calendar-year income, tax-claimer cash support, pregnant-woman household size, CHIP uninsured and premium rules, and uninsured-woman status.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines MAGI terms for MO HealthNet, establishes eligible coverage groups and MAGI equivalent net income thresholds effective January 1, 2014, mandates chapter 536 rulemaking with nonseverability, and directs federal state plan amendment and waiver submissions.

headings.title: Definitions for MAGI income eligibility determinations
headings.reviewNote: Defines child, CHIP-eligible children, department, modified adjusted gross income (MAGI), and MAGI equivalent net income standard for this section and section 208.990.

headings.title: Eligible coverage groups, MAGI income thresholds, and benefits
headings.reviewNote: Lists nine MO HealthNet coverage groups effective January 1, 2014, sets MAGI equivalent net income standards by group (1996 AFDC, 133 percent FPL, section 208.633, and 185 percent FPL), and provides section 208.152 benefits.

headings.title: Mandatory rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department or divisions to promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 and makes the section nonseverable from legislative rule-review powers after August 28, 2013.

headings.title: Submission of federal state plan amendments and waivers
headings.reviewNote: Requires DSS to submit necessary state plan amendments and waivers to CMS to implement this section.
